picks.blurb: Iowa State Football vs. UCF Knights: 3 Bold Predictions Skip to main content SI.COM Featured Stories Cyclones in the Pros The Iowa State Cyclones are riding some positive momentum into their Week 12 matchup against the UCF Knights. Last weekend, the Cyclones dominated the Cincinnati Bearcats at Jack Trice Stadium, winning 41-13. That evened their record out at 5-5 on the year, moving them one game away from becoming bowl-eligible. They will look to accomplish that feat on the road against a UCF squad that is also 5-5 on the season, with a marquee victory over the BYU Cougars when they were undefeated and the No. 2 team in the country. How will this Friday night game in Orlando turn out? Here are some bold predictions for the contest. Aiden Flora Held in Check Nov 14, 2026; Ames, Iowa, USA; Iowa State Cyclones running back Aiden Flora (21) strikes the Heisman Pose after scoring against the Cincinnati Bearcats at Jack Trice Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Reese Strickland-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The leading rusher in the country, Aiden Flora, has turned into a bona fide star for Iowa State. He has been dominant during Big 12 play , but he is going to be challenged by a stout Knights run defense. The leading rusher in the country, Aiden Flora, has turned into a bona fide star for Iowa State. He has been dominant during Big 12 play , but he is going to be challenged by a stout Knights run defense. UCF has one of the top-ranked run defenses in the country, coming in at No. 20 in the nation with a run defense grade of 91.2. Finding room is going to be a challenge for a team that ranks near the bottom of the country in run blocking, with the Cyclones earning a woeful 55.1 run-blocking grade. Knowing the success Flora has had, the lack of success in the trenches for the Iowa State offensive line to open lanes is shocking. Flora is going to handle a heavy workload, but he will be held in check as his streak of 175+ yard games will come to an end. But he will still have a solid game with 125 rushing yards. Defense Continues Trending in the Right Direction The Cyclones' defense has been challenged throughout the season, with all of their Power Conference opponents being ranked in the top 80 in points per drive . That streak will continue against the Knights, but Iowa State will have answers for them. An injury to quarterback Alonza Barnett III has kept UCF from truly reaching its potential. Riding some positive momentum after holding Cincinnati to 13 points, Jesse Bobbit's unit will continue that success against the Knights, who don’t excel along the offensive line. The Knights are ranked 108th with a pass-blocking grade of 57.2 and they are 115th in run-blocking with a grade of 54.3. Iowa State isn’t elite as a run defense or pass rush, but they should have an edge in the trenches to take advantage of. The Cyclones will pick up a hard-fought win, 27-21. Jaylen Raynor will have two touchdowns, taking full advantage of the Knights’ defense, which will sell out to try to stop Flora, continuing his hot streak after a rocky start to his Iowa State tenure. For a rebuilding year, this has been a blast. UCF was the team that beat BYU right after the giant Cougar win over Notre Dame. It's been up and down, though, with some puzzling clunkers to go along with the five wins. Get this, though, and there's a shot at the program's first winning season since 2022. away.blurb: UCF Senior Ruled Out For Senior Knight vs. Iowa State: Injury Report Breakdown Skip to main content SI.COM In addition to only one defensive back being ruled out in UCF's Tuesday player availability report, the Knights are trending toward getting back their leading rusher against the Cyclones. The Knights are trending toward relief in the secondary, with both DJ Bell and Kahmel Johnson ruled probable in Tuesday's report. However, the unit won't be fully all-hands-on-deck, as Demari Henderson was ruled out . As for Bell, a senior, and Johnson, they are set to return to their rotational roles, barring any setbacks. Bell, after missing four games, would be back rotating with Jayden Bellamy and Antione Jackson . Johnson, after missing two games, would return as the backup nickelback behind Braeden Marshall . Three Knights were ruled questionable in Tuesday's report. Another senior that is questionable for Friday's Senior Knight game is linebacker Jayden Jennings , who, despite being on the Knights' reports for eight weeks of conference games, has always managed to play. He has only been designated questionable for one of these weeks before this one, however. So, should he miss Friday's game, Tackett Curtis and Jahleel Culbreath would be in line to take on greater roles in the Knights' linebacker rotation. Finally, after missing last weekend's game against Arizona State, Waden Charles has the chance to return after just a one-game absence. Should he be out for a second game, however, the Knights would still have several receiving threats in the form of Josh Derry , Tyren Hornes , Duane Thomas Jr. and tight end Caden Piening . WEDNESDAY UPDATE: Charles was upgraded to probable for the Knights' Wednesday report. Joining Bell and Johnson in getting designated probable are Piening and running back Duke Watson . The designation implies a likely chance for Watson, the Knights' leading rusher this season, to return after missing Saturday's game against Arizona State. However, should he suffer any setbacks, he has Taevion Swint and Landen Chambers behind him. home.headline: UCF Q&A: How does Lewis Carter’s return help the Knights?
home.blurb: “Lewis, like a lot of our guys, he's been out a long time,” said coach Scott Frost . “He’s going to continue to get better as he gets closer to 100% and shakes the rust off a little bit. He’s a great person and a great player. He’s one of our leaders and we’ve missed him.” Ex-UCF star Tacko Fall, now with 76ers, says time was right for NBA return Florida & Caribbean Experiences Branded Content Paid Partner Content Services About the Orlando Sentinel 🎁 Gift idea: Sentinel's 150th book This was supposed to be Lewis Carter ‘s breakout season. Instead, the UCF linebacker and team captain found himself on the sideline with an injury that cost him half the season. Carter, 22, returned against Arizona State on Saturday, playing for the first time since Sept. 19 against Georgia State. “I was flying around and had a lot of energy. It felt good,” said Carter, who finished with three tackles on 25 snaps. In Carter’s absence, transfer Tackett Curtis has emerged as the team’s leading tackler (67), along with Jahleel Culbreath (44), Jaden Jennings (23), and Cole Kozlowski (19), who returned after a court order in fall camp. Carter spent much of his time off the field mentoring his teammates. “I was being hands-on as much as I could within the meeting rooms and on the sidelines,” said Carter. “I was trying to be a voice for the guys throughout.” How important are turnovers against Iowa State? Iowa State has turned the ball over just nine times — tied for the second-fewest turnovers given up in the Big 12 this season. Meanwhile, UCF has struggled to create takeaways lately, failing to force a turnover for the second time in its last three games. The Knights are 1-9 under Frost when they don’t force a miscue, including an 0-3 mark this season. “At times, we’ve been really good and the games where we’ve gotten turnovers, we’ve won those games,” said Frost. “That’s no secret. That’s the biggest stat in football.” Frost credits the takeaways with not only giving the team much-needed momentum, but also shortening the field and giving the offense more chances to score. Something the Knights could use more of over the remaining two games. How can the Knights get more pressure on the quarterback? UCF has gone back-to-back games without sacking a quarterback for the first time since 2021. The Knights have 16 sacks heading into this week’s showdown, tied for the second-fewest in the Big 12 with Iowa State. “We’ve actually gotten a lot of pressure, but we haven’t gotten the sacks,” said Frost. “As far as affecting throws, our guys have been pretty good. We’ve just got to finish those plays. The Huskers get their shot against Ohio State in Lincoln on Senior Day. It’s the last home game of the year, and a win would change how a lot of fans feel about this season. On the Carriker Chronicles, Adam Carriker breaks down why Nebraska has a chance, what worries him most, and why he thinks this game could still be up for grabs in the fourth quarter. Nebraska’s shutout of Rutgers showed how good this defense can be. The running game also put together a complete performance, which gives the Huskers something to build on. But can they run the ball against Ohio State when the Buckeyes know it’s coming? Carriker wants Nebraska to run with a purpose and give Anthony Colandrea some quick answers in the passing game. Get the tight ends involved. Take a few shots downfield when the matchup is there. And when it’s third down, give Ohio State something it hasn’t already seen. At some point, somebody has to win a one-on-one matchup. The biggest question on defense is Jeremiah Smith. How does Rob Aurich keep a receiver that good from taking over the game? That job gets tougher with Andrew Marshall out. Carriker talks through how Nebraska can mix up its pressure and make Ohio State work for its yards. A couple of big plays can undo an otherwise good afternoon for the defense. The Huskers need to keep Smith from getting loose and give themselves a chance to get off the field on third down. Carriker also spends time on something that could decide a close game: where each team starts with the ball. Archie Wilson can help Nebraska by pinning Ohio State deep and making the Buckeyes drive the length of the field. A turnover could give the Huskers a short field, but Nebraska has to cash in when it gets to the red zone. And if the defense or special teams can put seven points on the board themselves, that changes what the offense has to do to win. Carriker’s four keys are to win in the margins, limit what Ohio State does best, win the fourth quarter, and score a touchdown on defense or special teams. He sees a real path to an upset with the way Nebraska’s defense has played, the progress in the run game, and a home crowd that wants to send the seniors out with a win. In the end, the Huskers have yet to show us they can put together four full quarters against a team as good as Ohio State and the Jeremiah Smith matchup and Marshall’s absence are hard for him to get past. The 7-3 Buckeyes climbed six spots to No. 14 in Tuesday’s playoff rankings , just outside the top 12. Lincoln is a tough place for that test. McElroy pointed out that opponents convert just under 24% of their third downs against Nebraska. The Huskers are also tied for third nationally in third- and fourth-down success rate allowed . McElroy didn’t spare the Buckeyes’ front either. “The offensive line just doesn’t move anybody off the ball,” he said, adding that Ohio State averages 4.1 yards per carry. That puts more of the load on Jeremiah Smith, the Heisman Trophy betting favorite with 1,317 receiving yards and 15 touchdowns. However, McElroy warned that a pass-heavy game plan is a bad sign for Ohio State. “When Ryan Day’s team throws it 40 or more times, he’s just 5-5,” he said. Can Nebraska pull the upset? Defensive tackle Jahsear Whittington, who leads the team with six sacks, left the Rutgers win with an apparent knee injury. “One of the main things from that game to take away is just the amount of guys that stepped up with injuries ,” Rhule said. Nebraska’s kicking is another worry, since the Huskers are 6 of 13 on field goals. McElroy said that when a drive stalls, “it’s a coin flip on whether or not they walk out with points.” McElroy picks Ohio State to win 19-17. “I do, however, think that Nebraska will make a mistake or two, which ultimately gives Ohio State the victory,” he said. In Week 12, against Ohio State, they may look to do the same. The task won't be easy, though, as NU is set to face the 12th-best run defense in college football. As interim offensive coordinator Glenn Thomas previewed Nebraska's Senior Day matchup with the Buckeyes, freshman running back Jamal Rule was among the players who earned his praise. Here's what Thomas had to say Tuesday about the Huskers' offensive approach heading into their final home game of 2026. Jamal Rule leads Nebraska with 635 rushing yards on 110 attempts. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Rule quickly adjusted to the college game, totaling 411 all-purpose yards and all six of his touchdowns through the first three games of his freshman campaign. An ankle injury in the first quarter against Michigan State then limited his production and impact until last week. Rule quickly adjusted to the college game, totaling 411 all-purpose yards and all six of his touchdowns through the first three games of his freshman campaign. An ankle injury in the first quarter against Michigan State then limited his production and impact until last week. The freshman bounced back in a big way against Rutgers , carrying the ball 22 times for 103 yards. When Thomas was asked about Rule's performance and recovery from the injury, he was was quick to praise his progress. “He’s been great,” Thomas said. “He’s really turned the corner and is running hard. What excites you as much as anything is his physicality, but also his ability to make some yards after contact. First play of the game, safety comes up and, you know, makes some contact, and he was able to get six or eight yards after that.” “Those are the things that we continue to try and promote and be aware of,” Thomas continued. “Cause, you know, if you block a four-yard run, you want to get six or eight; you don’t want to get a four-yard run. So, he brings that element to us, and I think that really creates an advantage for us as far as staying in front of the chains.” Gibson Pyle has played a combined 146 snaps over the last two weeks and has been charged with just one quarterback hurry during that time. | Nebraska Athletics NU's success on the ground was also aided by several offensive linemen who weren't in the starting lineup when the season began. While Thomas praised the entire unit, he singled out Gunnar Gottula and Gibson Pyle, who combined for 109 offensive snaps against Rutgers and allowed just one pressure between them in Saturday's win. While Thomas praised the entire unit, he singled out Gunnar Gottula and Gibson Pyle, who combined for 109 offensive snaps against Rutgers and allowed just one pressure between them in Saturday's win. “Man, that’s been a nice advantage,” he said. “We really have a lot of flexibility on the offensive line with Gunnar. Gibby got in there and played a bunch; you know, in the last couple of games, he’s played quite a bit. So, there’s a lot of confidence in those guys when they come in, and I don’t feel like we’ve missed a beat with those guys.” The Huskers ran for 237 yards and two touchdowns on 43 rushing attempts against the Scarlet Knights. While Rutgers' defense ranked last in the Big Ten against the run, Nebraska's offensive line and running backs still deserve credit. That’s the game within the game, as far as trying to put those guys in a position; the best possible way to have success.” Carter Nelson has caught four passes for 88 yards and two touchdowns in Nebraska's last three games. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Nebraska's play-action passing game also found success against Rutgers, as in-state products Carter Nelson and Luke Lindenmeyer each hauled in a touchdown. While Lindenmeyer has been a reliable contributor for several years, Nelson has emerged as a welcome addition in recent weeks. “I think he’s a new player,” Thomas said regarding the former No. 3 tight end in the 2024 recruiting class. “I’m super excited for where he’s at, not only off the field, but on the field. He’s really taken the next step since the injury. He’s playing fast; he’s playing confident; he’s physical. “He’s still a work in progress as far as having, you know, all the offseason, lack of reps. So, he’s continued to grow within the season, and it’s been exciting to see, and that has translated to the field.” While Thomas noted that Nelson needs to work on his throwing motion following his failed pass attempt on a fake punt against Rutgers, it's clear the Huskers plan to utilize him more as a receiving threat. Players like Nelson, Rule, and Pyle are continuing to develop before our eyes, and Nebraska will need each of them to step up against Ohio State. Kickoff for Saturday's contest is set for 11 a.m. Central, with the Huskers entering the matchup as slight underdogs. How well those players handle their expanded roles could go a long way toward determining NU's chances of pulling off the upset. We'll find out how they fare soon enough. With plenty to get to, I broke down three of Saturday's biggest games and came through with at least one pick for each matchup. It begins at noon ET, as the No. 14 Ohio State Buckeyes head to Lincoln as short favorites to take on the Nebraska Cornhuskers . After that, we'll stay in the Big Ten, where the Washington Huskies host the No. 8 Indiana Hoosiers , who are looking to prove they belong higher in the CFP rankings. To close it all out, we have a huge SEC showdown between the No. 1 Georgia Bulldogs and No. 21 South Carolina Gamecocks . Ohio State vs. Nebraska Pick Ohio State Buckeyes Quarterback Luke Fahey continues to lead Ohio State through a top Big Ten ranking in scoring and total offense. The freshman signal-caller played his first clean game from a turnover-worthy play perspective against Northwestern , connecting for 201 passing yards and three touchdown s. There has been no shortage of targets for Heisman contender Jeremiah Smith , generating a season-high 17 targets against the Wildcats . Smith continues to build a case as the best player in college football, and he's now up to 15 touchdowns and an elite four yards per route run on the season. While Fahey has seen 37 pressures in three starts under center, the defense has failed to create pressure. Ohio State has just 16 sacks on the season after an outburst of five against Northwestern. Despite a low amount of pressure for coordinator Matt Patricia, the defense has been one of the best in the country at stopping the rush, dominating offenses that elect to use zone read with a 50% Success Rate . Passing downs have not been friendly to Ohio State, though, ranking outside the top 100 in EPA allowed alongside a third-down conversion allowed rank of 86th. Nebraska Cornhuskers Head coach Matt Rhule shook up the offense after four consecutive losses, firing coordinator Dana Holgorsen. Nebraska scored a grand total of 23 points in the second half of all four losses . The Cornhuskers responded with a 31-0 victory over Rutgers , a road trip that included 17 points in the second half. The top advantage for Nebraska has been the ability to create explosive plays on the ground, ranking sixth in Rush EPA. Quarterback Anthony Colandrea leads the team in 10-yard gains with 22, while running back Jamal Rule's elusiveness has forced 25 missed tackles and 4.7 yards after first contact. Coordinator Rob Aurich has created a menacing Cornhusker defense that has allowed less than 15 points a game with top-35 ranks in Success Rate allowed and Methodical Drives allowed. The defense has shut down opposing passing attacks from creating explosives, ranking fifth in EPA allowed. The pass rush is led by edge Williams Nwaneri and interior Jahsear Whittington, both providing 20 pressures apiece. The rush defense has taken the largest step forward, as Nebraska ranks 20th in Line Yards compared to a number outside the top 100 a year ago. Ohio State vs Nebraska Prediction The Ohio State offense will have trouble establishing the run out of the gate with running back Bo Jackson. More than 70% of the running back's rushing attempts come through zone read. Ohio State prefers to run inside zone with 11 personnel while using a two-tight end set for outside zone. The Cornhusker defense has respectable numbers against inside zone at a 55% Success Rate, creating a higher number of 58% against opponents using 12 personnel with outside zone . Colandrea should have a pressure-free game, with the Huskers' offensive line sitting top-10 in pressure rate allowed. The former UNLV and Virginia quarterback has a small 2% turnover-worthy play rate in a clean pocket, enough to execute in the pass game. The biggest advantage for Nebraska comes with big plays on the ground, as its Rush EPA rank of sixth flies directly into an Ohio State defense that ranks 79th in Rush EPA allowed. The game for Nebraska's offense will be decided in counter concepts, generating an explosive on 22% of its 77 rushing attempts. Action Network's Betting Power Ratings call for Ohio State at -3.5, a number spot-on with the current market. This will be Fahey's second road game as the Buckeyes' starter after he posted zero big-time throws at USC . The Huskers' ability to generate rush explosives against an Ohio State defense that fails to create a pass rush will be the difference in Lincoln. The Buckeyes looked unprepared, sloppy, and undisciplined en route to a 30-18 loss in L.A., and followed that up with an u ninspiring beatdown at the hands of Oregon in Columbus to the tune of 41-28. However, the Buckeyes bounced back last week and took down Northwestern 28-19 to get back on track. Next up is a road trip to Nebraska before things close out at home vs. -- ahem, you know -- Michigan . And now, thanks to the latest College Football Playoff rankings, it sure feels like Ohio State is in the mix to get into the playoff if it wins out and gets a little help. In fact, Ohio State checked in at No. 14 in the third release of the rankings just released on Tuesday, and that's six spots higher already than the week prior and just three spots away from making the 12-team field. According to the analytics ESPN uses to predict the chances of victory, Ohio State has a 71.3% chance of beating the Cornhuskers . That's good and fine, but we have to remember that this same model had the Buckeyes with a significant chance of beating the Trojans on the road, and then the Ducks at home, and neither of those turned out so well. Hopefully, the worldwide leader has this one right just like last week, and we can be celebrating a much-needed win to set up a matchup against Michigan that could be bigger than we thought just a couple of weeks ago. Since these analytics are updated by game results only, there's no chance of this percentage changing, but the Buckeyes will still need to execute at a high level, help out freshman quarterback Luke Fahey , and not make as many mental mistakes, especially on the road. The game is set to kick off at Noon ET on Fox, and we'll have more on the game leading up to Saturday, and be around during and after as well for extensive coverage. Hopefully, we are setting the stage for "The Game" with some things on the line. picks.blurb: Ohio State vs. Nebraska Final Score Predictions: Can the Buckeyes keep slim College Football Playoff hopes alive? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football CFP And Bowl Games James Harden drops 51 in Cavs’ NBA Cup win over Pacers TRENDING Maye reportedly fractures fibula Report: Dodgers get Royce Lewis Kane to miss multiple months Puka Nacua suspended 'GTA 6' impacts sports Vincent Carchietta-Imagn Images | Adam Cairns/Columbus Dispatch-Imagn Images Brandon Little, Craig Smith, Rob Gregson, Ryan Roberts, Tyler Forness · AtoZ Sports Thu, November 19, 2026 at 6:04 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The A to Z Sports college football staff takes a crack at predicting the result of Ohio State vs. Nebraska in Week 12. The Ohio State Buckeyes moved up to No. 14 in the College Football Playoff rankings following a win over Northwestern this week. Now, they are on the road in another must-win situation against Nebraska . Nebraska has lost four of its last five games after a good start to the season, and it just hasn't been the same team. Still, there's always a home-field advantage in Lincoln, and this should be a good one. Ahead of the game, those who cover college football at A to Z Sports weigh in on how this one will play out. Ohio State 30, Nebraska 23 Ohio State finally got back in the win column last weekend with a win over Northwestern, which was its first since Week 7 against Indiana. The two losses that followed hurt the Buckeyes badly, and they sit at three losses on the season with a minimal chance of reaching the College Football Playoff. Ohio State's defense hasn't been the same in weeks, though it did show some life against Northwestern, at least, without Aidan Chiles. Ohio State has a 35% chance to make the College Football Playoff and a 1% chance to win the national title, according to the A to Z Sports CFB Playoff Predictor (updated November 15, 2026). Nebraska is going to want to run the ball and lean on its top-10 defense against Ohio State. It's important for the Buckeyes to get off to a strong start in this one to put the Cornhuskers in situations where they need to pass the football to get back into it. Freshman quarterback Luke Fahey doesn't have a road win yet, so going on the road and showing his ability is going to be key. The Buckeyes will be healthier along the offensive line with Luke Montgomery back, which will certainly help the run game. Ohio State wins what will be another close one in Lincoln. - Brandon Little, A to Z Sports Ohio State Ohio State 35, Nebraska 17 Tuesday night proved that Ohio State still has a chance at the postseason, albeit a small chance. The Buckeyes need to win out and get some help from the teams directly in front of them, but the sport has been a wild ride this season, so anything is possible. The same way that Nebraska beating Ohio State is possible. But that's not going to happen. UNLV transfer QB Anthony Colandrea has had a nice season for the Cornhuskers, but I don't believe that Nebraska has the offensive firepower to keep up with Ohio State. The defense has kept things tight throughout the season, but they have yet to play a Jeremiah Smith. Give me OSU comfortably a week before the big one. - Rob Gregson, A to Z Sports Alabama Ohio State 27, Nebraska 10 The Buckeyes showed some signs of life against Northwestern this past week, and it's gotten them back into the College Football Playoff conversation. Luckily for them, they are getting Nebraska after they have lost a few close Big Ten games, and they feel relatively lost right now. This is exactly what Luke Fahey needs going into the stretch run, and it could end up his best showing yet leading Ohio State's offense. - Tyler Forness, A to Z Sports Florida Ohio State 34, Nebraska 14 Ohio State's offense finds its rhythm in a convincing 34-14 win over Nebraska. The Cornhuskers' offensive struggles continue to be a major problem, as they have difficulty sustaining drives and putting consistent pressure on the Buckeyes' defense. Nebraska simply doesn't have enough answers offensively to keep pace with an Ohio State team that can create explosive plays and capitalize on mistakes. The Buckeyes should be able to control the game for much of the afternoon, forcing Nebraska into uncomfortable passing situations and limiting its opportunities to make things interesting. On the other side, Jeremiah Smith continues to look like one of the most dominant players in college football. Nebraska has a difficult time finding an answer for his combination of size, speed and playmaking ability, and he comes through with another big performance. Luke Fahey also shows some encouraging growth at quarterback for Ohio State. He doesn't have to be spectacular, but making better decisions, showing more confidence and taking advantage of opportunities downfield would be a positive step. Ohio State is the more talented and complete team, and that shows up on the scoreboard. - Ryan Roberts, A to Z Sports Notre Dame Ohio State 23, Nebraska 13 Ohio State got a big jump this week in the rankings after a but of a shaky but good enough performance against an undermanned Northwestern team last Saturday. Now they go back on the road against a Nebraska team that just snapped a four-game losing streak with a 31-0 win over Rutgers last weekend. They failed to eclipse 17 points during that losing streak. I don't see them doing much better against an Ohio State defense that has been mortal in recent weeks, but has enough talent to give the Cornhuskers fits. It's not emphatic, but it's just good enough for Ryan Day's team to stay in the playoff mix heading into The Game. - Craig Smith, A to Z Sports Miami This article was originally published on A to Z Sports. home.headline: Nebraska’s OSU injury report is rough, but Anthony Jones' return could be bright spot
home.blurb: Defensive back Andrew Marshall is out , as Matt Rhule announced earlier this week that one of the nation's top cornerbacks will miss the rest of Nebraska’s season. The good news for the Huskers is that defensive lineman Anthony Jones Jr. was upgraded from “out” last week to “questionable” this week. With this being the first injury report of the week, there’s now hope that he could be upgraded to probable by Friday and then suit up on Saturday morning. For Ohio State, the guys who are out were all expected to be out. Quarterback Julian Sayin, running back Ja'Kobi Jackson, safety Deshawn Stewart, wide receiver Brennen Schramm, offensive linemen Jaxon Powell and Max Riley, and tight end Maxence LeBlanc will miss the game against the Cornhuskers. Nebraska football loses Owen Chambliss, Jahsear Whittington but Anthony Jones could return The Ohio State players who are questionable are safety Terry Moore, wide receiver Brock Boyd, safety Brenten "Inky" Jones, linebacker Eli Lee, and offensive lineman Phillip Daniels. The biggest piece of positive news for the Buckeyes is that senior left guard Luke Montgomery is expected to return. Montgomery is ready to roll after not appearing on the report, while both Daniels and Boyd are listed as questionable. Montgomery and Daniels had flu-like symptoms last week, while Boyd has been battling a sprained ankle for more than a month. No surprises popped up on the availability report for Ohio State, unlike last week when Montgomery was initially listed as questionable. That suggests the Buckeyes avoided any major new injuries in their win over Northwestern. Of course, the biggest absence of all for OSU is quarterback Julian Sayin. That might not be as big a problem for Ryan Day and company after his replacement, Luke Fahey , finally had a very solid outing. Against Northwestern, Fahey completed 21 of 32 passes for 201 yards and 3 touchdowns. He also threw an interception, but the biggest step forward was that he seemed to figure out a secret to the offense: Just get the ball to Jeremiah Smith. Without Owen Chambliss, Jahsear Whittington, and Andrew Marshall, Nebraska will have its work cut out for it on Saturday morning. The undefeated fifth-ranked Boilermakers led No. 10 Wisconsin 17-14 in a nationally televised game (back when that wasn't the norm) and with ESPN College Gameday set up on campus. Kyle Orton ran a naked bootleg on third down, seemingly keeping the drive alive for Purdue to burn more clock, only Orton was hit, jarring the ball loose. Scott Starks picked it up and returned it 40 yards for a touchdown. After Bernard Pollard blocked the extra point, the Boilers drove into field goal range but missed a game-tying field goal attempt in the final minute. Wisconsin escaped Ross-Ade Stadium with a 20-17 victory , its first in what is now a string of 18 consecutive Badger victories in the series. On Saturday, Purdue coach Barry Odom gets his first chance to end more than two decades of coming up on the wrong side against the Badgers . "The great thing is this team had nothing to do with that. But it is history. I What to knthink you always learn from those things. You take those things and use it as needed or as you think your current team needs." Odom's timeframe is off. He was a sophomore linebacker at Missouri when Purdue defeated Wisconsin 45-20 at Ross-Ade Stadium in 1997, but his point was made. It's been a long time. What to know about Purdue football's opponent, Wisconsin The Badgers are 6-4, coming off a loss to Maryland in what has been an up-and-down season that includes a 24-7 win over USC on Oct. 24. Wisconsin allows just 17 points per game, problematic for a Purdue offense that has both looked phenomenal and, more recently, shown an inability to capitalize in the red zone. Wisconsin is allowing just 2.8 yards per carry this season, aided by the Badgers' 20 sacks. Hopkins is listed as questionable entering Saturday's game. Hopkins was elevated to starting quarterback to replace the struggling Colton Joseph two weeks ago. picks.headline: 3 Bold Predictions for Wisconsin vs. Purdue: Don't Count out Colton Joseph Just Yet
picks.blurb: 3 Bold Predictions for Wisconsin vs. Purdue: Don't Count out Colton Joseph Just Yet - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football CFP And Bowl Games James Harden drops 51 in Cavs’ NBA Cup win over Pacers TRENDING Maye reportedly fractures fibula Report: Dodgers get Royce Lewis Kane to miss multiple months Puka Nacua suspended 'GTA 6' impacts sports Wisconsin Badgers quarterback Colton Joseph. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Seamus Rohrer · Wisconsin Badgers On SI Thu, November 19, 2026 at 7:30 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads As the Badgers' seesaw of a 2026 season rolls on, Wisconsin once finds itself on the wrong end of a tough loss after collapsing on the road against Maryland . Sitting at 6-4 (4-3 in the B1G), head coach Luke Fickell and company are running out of time to prove that they're guiding this program in the right direction. A resounding win over an inferior opponent , bouncing back from a mind-numbing loss in the process, would be a great start. I've got three bold predictions for the Badgers' clash with the Boilermakers in West Lafayette. Colton Joseph recaptures the hearts of Badgers fans Wisconsin Badgers quarterback Colton Joseph. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Ryan Hopkins is currently listed as questionable this week, but the early indications are that Joseph is going to re-assume the QB1 role after Hopkins took a huge blindside hit and had to be helped off the field late in the loss to Maryland. If Joseph indeed gets the starting nod in place of an injured Hopkins, it's not hard to see him playing well and in the process, winning back the hearts of some Badgers fans despite his well-documented struggles this season. First of all, Joseph should have no shortage of motivation. He was benched for a true freshman, and now gets his shot to prove that was a big mistake. That's a situation any competitor dreams of, and say what you will about Joseph; he's certainly a competitor. What's more, after getting benched for Hopkins and with the future of the entire coaching staff potentially up in the air this offseason, Joseph needs to put good things on tape should he be forced to enter the transfer portal again this winter. At best, he's proved dynamic yet inconsistent at the Big Ten level and at worst, he's been a turnover machine with limited arm talent. If Hopkins is forced to sit out one or both of the final two games this fall, these contests are massively important for Joseph's future; how he plays could determine whether he remains at the Power Four level in 2027. Finally, Purdue's defense is extremely permeable . It has the worst total defense in the Big Ten (417.3 yards per game) and the second-worst passing defense in the conference (239.0 yards per game). Purdue struggles to get consistent pressure (13 sacks across 10 games) and doesn't force turnovers with regularity. If there's any defense for Joseph to carve through, it's the Boilermakers. Wisconsin shuts down another prolific passer Purdue Boilermakers quarterback Ryan Browne. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Purdue's Ryan Browne is second in the Big Ten and 20th nationally with 2,418 passing yards. Though Purdue scores 27.2 points per game, a meager 76th in the country, its quarterback has been a bright spot in terms of offensive production. Still, dive into Browne's performance this season, and the numbers are a tad misleading. The quarterback hasn't eclipsed 300 passing yards since Week 3 against UCLA, and while that's certainly an impressive feat given how strong the Bruins' defense is, he's struggled pretty mightily against the other top defenses he's faced. In fact, Browne has been held under 160 passing yards in four of his last seven outings. Against the top passing defenses he's played such as Penn State (No. 3 nationally in passing yards allowed per game) as well as Iowa and Minnesota (both of whom rank inside the top-45 in passing yards allowed), he's had a rough go of it. The Nittany Lions held him to 142 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions on 34 percent completion. Iowa limited him to 158 yards, one touchdown and one interceptions. And while Purdue blew out Minnesota, Brown only collected 159 passing yards, one score and 58 percent completion. Wisconsin's pass defense, meanwhile, checks in at No. 25 in the country. And while it just allowed Maryland's backup to complete 21-of-23 passes last week, the Badgers' defense has managed to bounce back from its poor performances this season. It'll need to run it back in West Lafayette. The Badgers' offensive line looks passable This might be the boldest prediction of the three, considering how much of a struggle its been up front for Wisconsin. Last week against Maryland, the Badgers' offensive line struggled mightily in pass protection, allowing four sacks. It wasn't much better in the run game, as Wisconsin backs created just 3.3 yards per carry and also suffered six tackles-for-loss. Still, Maryland's lowly record did well to disguise just how capable its front seven actually is. For how bad the Terps have been this fall, their defensive front is pretty loaded with capable playmakers. The same can't be said for Purdue. The Boilermakers have just 13 sacks on the season, firmly placing them into the bottom tier of teams; only 14 FBS programs have fewer. They've created 107 total pressures, which is harder to contextualize nationally but compared with Wisconsin's 145 total pressures, they're a clear step down. Their run defense, meanwhile, surrenders 178.3 yards per game, good for 110th nationally. Their defense as a whole has collected 205 stops, or tackles that constitute a failure for the offense, compared to Wisconsin's 276. Translation? They don't penetrate the backfield or win at the point of attack nearly as well as the Badgers. Despite what could be a patchwork offensive line this week, I still expect Wisconsin to find success up front. Wisconsin's initial injury report lists starting cornerback and the Badgers' best cover man in the secondary, Javan Robinson, as doubtful for Saturday afternoon. That means barring a significant development, Wisconsin will be without its top cornerback and another veteran leader in the secondary. Starting quarterback Ryan Hopkins, who Fickell sounded encouraged about on Monday, is listed as questionable. Right now, it looks like a toss-up if he'll be able to play despite Fickell saying earlier in the week that "Hopefully he'll be fine...luckily it's not his throwing side." Wisconsin's starting right tackle Emerson Mandell is also listed as questionable. He wasn't noticeably banged up last week against the Terps, so Fickell wasn't asked about his status on Monday. However, he's now a question mark as well, and with Barrett Nelson also unavailable for the past three weeks, Wisconsin could be forced to start a tackle tandem of PJ Wilkins and Lucas Simmons-Johansson. That's certainly less than ideal, although the latter did just play a career-high 26 snaps against Maryland. Though Robinson almost certainly being out and the uncertainty around Hopkins and Mandell is disheartening, the Badgers did receive some good news on the injury front. Their other starting cornerback Jai'mier Scott, who didn't play last week in College Park, is listed as probable, as is star pass-rusher Sebastian Cheeks. Getting those two back would do wonders to mitigate the damage this defense has already suffered. Regardless of how the week shakes out, Wisconsin is going to have to take down Purdue somewhat short-handed. Wisconsin Football is Running Out of Time to Fix its Ground Game Other than the constant shuffling on the offensive line, much of which was caused at least initially by injuries suffered before the season began, Wisconsin football has had a relatively clean bill of health for much of the year, especially considering head coach Luke Fickell's past injury luck in Madison. When Wisconsin (6-4, 4-3 B1G) travels to face Purdue (3-7, 2-5 B1G) on Saturday afternoon in West Lafayette, it could be without several key starters in a game that's critically important for Fickell and company to bounce back and win after the late collapse in College Park last weekend. We already knew that starting safety Matt Jung was lost for the season, joining the likes of offensive tackle Kevin Heywood and cornerback Cai Bates. But the Badgers' initial injury report poses more questions than answers ahead of a game against Purdue in which, again, Wisconsin could really use a bounce-back victory on the road. home.headline: Ryan Hopkins headlines first Wisconsin vs. Purdue availability report
home.blurb: However, Luke Fickell and Co. didn’t just leave SECU Stadium with a bruised ego, as newly-donned starting quarterback Ryan Hopkins was recently listed as questionable in Wisconsin’s latest injury availability report ahead of this weekend’s clash against the Purdue Boilermakers . The Wisconsin Badgers are stumbling to the end of the 2026 football season, as their 24-21 loss against the Maryland Terrapins last weekend did them no favors. What does this mean for Wisconsin’s quarterback situation? In Hopkins’ two starts for the Badgers , the Mater Dei product tallied 318 yards through the air, on a 63% completion rate, along with three touchdowns and two fumbles. In Wisconsin’s last-second loss to the Terps, Hopkins finished with just 55 yards in the air, continuing a trend of disappointing quarterback play in 2026. If Hopkins is unable to go, it's plausible that original starter Colton Joseph gets the start, as the former Old Dominion quarterback has totaled 1,739 all-purpose yards, along with 15 total touchdowns and six turnovers. Keys, prediction for Tar Heels vs Cavaliers Rodd Baxley, Fayetteville Observer · The Fayetteville Observer Fri, November 20, 2026 at 10:05 AM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads UNC football has two more opportunities to secure bowl eligibility in its second season under coach Bill Belichick . The next chance comes in the latest edition of "The South's Oldest Rivalry" as the Tar Heels (5-5, 2-4 ACC) travel to Virginia (5-5, 3-4) for an ACC game at Scott Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 21. Kickoff is set for 12:30 p.m. and the game will be televised on The CW . Watch UNC-Virginia on Fubo BOWL PROJECTIONS: Will UNC football make postseason? Latest bowl projections before Virginia game INJURY REPORT: Who is on UNC football vs Virginia injury report? Latest from ACC availability report POSTGAME BRAWL: ACC announces suspensions, fines for UNC football and Louisville after postgame fight UNC has a 4-1 record away from Chapel Hill this season, including a season-opening win against TCU in Ireland. The Tar Heels have won three straight road games since a mid-September loss at Clemson. UNC has also won consecutive games on Virginia's home field. If it stretches that streak to three, it would be the first time since 2016. Overall, the Tar Heels have a 28-27 record at Virginia. Here are some stats to know, players to watch and a score prediction for the Tar Heels vs. Cavaliers. Billy Edwards or Travis Burgess as UNC quarterback vs Virginia? Who will be UNC's starting quarterback vs. Virginia? That's the biggest question surrounding this game. A sixth-year player who started the first 10 games of the season, Billy Edwards Jr. was listed as questionable on the initial ACC availability report . That could open the door for freshman QB Travis Burgess to get his first career start. Burgess replaced Edwards in the second half of the Tar Heels' loss to Louisville, leading a late scoring drive that gave UNC an opportunity to win in the fourth quarter. If Burgess does get the start, he would be the first true freshman to start at QB for UNC in an ACC game since Sam Howell in 2019. UNC defense faces challenge vs Virginia QB Beau Pribula without Greg Smith UNC's defense is arguably coming off its best performance of the season, limiting a Louisville offense that averaged more than 40 points per game to 16 at Kenan Stadium. The Tar Heels won't face that level of explosiveness against Virginia, but it could be tough because of the absence of two key players. Defensive back Greg Smith and defensive lineman Melkart Abou Jaoude are among the Tar Heels out vs. the Cavaliers, but Smith is only out for the first half for his role in the postgame brawl vs. Louisville. In Virginia's wins, quarterback Beau Pribula is averaging 171 passing yards and 45 rushing yards with 11 passing TDs, one rushing TD and one interception. In five losses, Pribula is averaging 174 passing yards and 7 rushing yards with four passing TDs, two interceptions and a rushing TD. If UNC can bottle up Pribula, it'll likely leave Charlottesville its sixth win of the season. UNC running back Benjamin Hall gets redemption shot vs Virginia Benjamin Hall was just short of the goal line on a two-point conversion that would have given UNC its first signature win under Bill Belichick in 2025. The Tar Heels lost 17-16 to No. 16 Virginia in overtime last season at Kenan Stadium . With three touchdowns in the last two weeks, including a two-TD effort vs. Louisville, Hall will have a chance at redemption on Saturday at Scott Stadium. The junior running back's two best games of the season came on the road. Hall logged 130 rushing yards and a receiving TD at Clemson and racked up 81 rushing yards and a TD on nine carries at UConn. UNC vs Virginia score prediction UNC 22, Virginia 18: The Tar Heels have been a different team on the road this season, finding ways to win by creating takeaways and scoring on explosive plays. Even with its questions at QB, UNC seems to get a jolt away from Chapel Hill. Belichick's boys will be celebrating in Charlottesville after securing bowl eligibility ahead of the regular-season finale. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect North Carolina vs Virginia Prediction 11/21/2026 Today's College Football Picks Chris Ruffolo North Carolina Tar Heels Virginia Cavaliers Over 41.5 (-112) Under 41.5 (-108) Scott Stadium, Charlottesville, VA Saturday, November 21, 2026 Ron Romanelli Big Al McMordie See the full rankings: Best College Football Handicappers North Carolina Tar Heels vs. Virginia Cavaliers Prediction I'm taking North Carolina and the points against Virginia. Both teams are 5-5 and need one more win to get bowl eligible, but I think the Tar Heels are in the better spot, even on the road. Virginia finally put together a convincing performance against Cal, and congratulations on that, but one good Saturday doesn't erase how rough conference play has been for the Cavaliers. North Carolina hasn't exactly been reliable at home, either. The difference is that the Tar Heels have actually played some of their best football away from Chapel Hill, and I think that travels to Charlottesville. North Carolina is 3-1 in true road games, with wins at Pitt, Duke and UConn. The Pitt and Duke wins came by four points apiece, and the Tar Heels followed them with a 38-21 victory at UConn. That's not a murderer's row, but winning three straight road games is hard to dismiss when we're talking about a matchup priced essentially as a toss-up. Compare that with North Carolina's recent home form: losses to Syracuse, Miami and Louisville in three of its last four games. The results haven't always been pretty, but the road version of this team has been more dependable. Virginia's 36-7 win over Cal looks great on the scoreboard, although it's worth remembering that two of the Cavaliers' touchdowns came on interception returns. That was a much-needed response after losing three straight to SMU, Duke and Wake Forest, including a 51-7 beating at Wake. I've been waiting for Virginia's veteran offensive line to become a consistent strength, but it hasn't happened. The Cavaliers have struggled to protect Beau Pribula and are converting only about 32 percent of third downs. That's a major problem against a North Carolina defense that just showed it can make a good offense work. The Tar Heels lost 16-14 to Louisville last week, but I thought the defense deserved a lot more credit than the final result suggests. Louisville came in averaging more than 40 points and nearly eight yards per play. North Carolina held the Cardinals to 302 yards, just 4.7 per play, and only one gain of more than 20 yards. Derek McDonald has been all over the field with 101 tackles on the season. If that defense shows up again, Virginia isn't suddenly going to find easy yards just because it's playing its home finale. There is one legitimate concern for North Carolina, and that's the quarterback situation. Billy Edwards Jr. left the Louisville game injured and was listed as questionable, while freshman Travis Burgess came in and showed some mobility but also threw an interception. I'm not going to pretend that uncertainty doesn't matter. Still, Virginia has been vulnerable to mobile quarterbacks, and Burgess at least gives the Tar Heels a different way to move the chains if he's needed. North Carolina is also converting around 46 percent of its third downs, compared with Virginia's much lower rate, which is a meaningful difference in a game where possessions could be limited. Virginia is 5-1 at Scott Stadium, and this is Senior Day, so the Cavaliers absolutely have a home-field argument. Pribula can hurt opponents with his legs, too, and Virginia's plus-six turnover margin is better than North Carolina's minus-three. Those are real reasons this isn't a slam dunk. But the Cavaliers have struggled to finish drives, scoring on roughly 73 percent of their red-zone trips, while North Carolina has converted better than 90 percent of its opportunities. With neither offense consistently explosive, missed chances inside the twenty could matter as much as the occasional big play. Chris Ruffolo's Pick: North Carolina +1.5 Need More? away.headline: North Carolina's Neo Avdalas Receives Brutal Injury Update
away.blurb: Through four games, Denis is averaging 8.5 points, 3.5 rebounds, 2.8 assists, and a steal per game, shooting 33.3 percent from the field and 38.9 percent from beyond the arc. North Carolina's Neo Avdalas Receives Brutal Injury Update TarHeelsRoundtable 160 Members • 1,672 Posts TarHeelsRoundtable TarHeelsRoundtable Related stories IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect North Carolina's Neo Avdalas Receives Brutal Injury Update Ben Cooper Partner Nov 17, 2026 7:30 PM Published Nov 17, 2026 7:30 PM North Carolina Tar Heels guard Neo Avdalas received an unfortunate update on his injury. The North Carolina Tar Heels are off to a 3-1 start to the 2026-27 season in their first year under head coach Michael Malone. It's a solid start for Malone's team, but they are dealing with a disappointing injury, as guard Neo Avdalas is expected to miss at least two months with a broken wrist . In four games with the Tar Heels, Avdalas averaged nine points, 3.5 rebounds, and 3.8 assists per game, shooting 40.6 percent from the field and 20 percent from three. He was going to be a key playmaker for North Carolina and will be a significant absence in their lineup over the next couple of months. Avdalas spent his freshman season at Virginia Tech, averaging 12.1 points, 3.1 rebounds, and 4.6 assists per game, shooting 38.6 percent from the floor and 31.4 percent from deep. It was a solid freshman campaign, and he was poised to be a pivotal piece in the Tar Heels' rotation. During his absence, North Carolina will lean on Isaiah Denis, Matt Able, and Terrence Brown to step up as playmakers. Able will also play a key role as a playmaker, as he's averaging 10.8 points, 2.5 rebounds, and 2.3 assists per game, shooting 44.1 percent from the floor and 30.4 percent from downtown. He is a solid scorer, but they will need him to pick up his playmaking over the next couple of months. North Carolina's top scorer, Brown, could also be needed to step up as a passer. He is averaging 17.5 points, 3.5 rebounds, 1.5 assists, and two steals per game, shooting 43.4 percent from the field and 38.5 percent from distance. North Carolina is looking to make a deep run in Malone's first year as their head coach. Malone had a successful tenure in the NBA, winning a championship with the Denver Nuggets. The Tar Heels went 24-9 in the 2025-26 season, but lost in the first round of the NCAA Tournament. North Carolina has a different roster and coaching staff this season and will look to be a contender to win the NCAA title, but will have to survive early in the season without Avdalas.

away.headline: North Carolina's Neo Avdalas to Miss Two Months With Wrist Injury
away.blurb: A potential two-month recovery timeline could put Avdalas in position to return around January, although North Carolina has not announced a specific return date. North Carolina's Neo Avdalas to Miss Two Months With Wrist Injury Football North Carolina basketball has suffered a significant setback early in the 2026-27 season, as sophomore guard Neo Avdalas is expected to miss approximately two months after suffering a fractured left wrist. The Tar Heels announced Tuesday that Avdalas underwent surgery to repair the injury. The sophomore suffered the injury during Friday night’s 78-70 loss to Georgia at the Dean E. Smith Center. Avdalas is expected to miss a significant portion of North Carolina’s nonconference schedule, along with the beginning of ACC play, as he begins his recovery. The injury is a tough blow for first-year head coach Michael Malone, who has relied on Avdalas as an important part of the Tar Heels’ backcourt rotation. Through North Carolina’s first four games, Avdalas averaged 9.0 points, 3.5 rebounds and a team-leading 3.8 assists per game. He also recorded 15 assists, the most on the team, while ranking fourth in scoring. Avdalas started all four games for the Tar Heels after transferring from Virginia Tech during the offseason. During his freshman season with the Hokies, the 6-foot-9 guard averaged 12.1 points and 4.6 assists per game. He started all 31 games and earned ACC Rookie of the Week honors twice. His size, versatility and playmaking ability made him an important addition to Malone’s first North Carolina roster. Tar Heels Must Adjust Without Neo Avdalas With Avdalas sidelined, North Carolina will need other players to take on additional responsibilities in the backcourt. Terrence Brown, Isaiah Denis, Angelo Brizzi and Jaydon Young could all see increased opportunities as the Tar Heels look to replace Avdalas’ production and playmaking. Brown has been one of North Carolina’s leading offensive contributors early in the season, while Denis has also provided valuable minutes in the backcourt. North Carolina enters the next stretch of its schedule at 3-1 following the loss to Georgia. The Tar Heels will look to get back on track when they host Marshall on Friday, Nov. 20. His absence will be an early test for Malone and the Tar Heels as they attempt to maintain momentum and navigate the opening portion of their ACC schedule without one of their key offseason additions. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect Transfer Portal 2027 Top Recruits 2027 Top Classes College Football Rankings The unbeaten Bruins can clinch a Big Ten title game berth, but the struggling Wolverines have a clear path to shock their new conference rival if they protect the football Getty Images Michigan has fallen so far under Kyle Whittingham that the all-time winningest program in college football has been reduced to being a home underdog against a UCLA program that won three games last season. The No. 4 Bruins are arriving for their first game at Michigan Stadium since 1996 on Saturday in prime position to reach the Big Ten Championship Game and College Football Playoff. The Wolverines team hosting them is scraping rock bottom after falling to 5-5 with a 31-7 loss at Oregon last week. It's a jarring backdrop for the first battle between these teams as Big Ten foes. At 10-0 (7-0 Big Ten), the Bruins are one win away from reaching 11 victories for the first time in program history. Just three years removed from a national championship, Michigan may be on the cusp of yet another coaching change. Lauded as a stabilizing hire amid a tumultuous ending to Sherrone Moore's tenure last year, Whittingham has presided over a disaster. Michigan ranks 131st of 138 FBS teams in total offense, averaging just 300.9 yards per game. While the Wolverines have quickly reached dire straits under Whittingham, 66, they can play the role of spoiler over the season's final two weeks. Handing UCLA its first loss and/or upsetting rival Ohio State to close the season would bring some morsel of satisfaction to what has been a painful 2026 slog in Ann Arbor. Michigan vs. UCLA: Need to know What's at stake for UCLA: Despite its 10-0 record, UCLA is still not a lock for the College Football Playoff. The Bruins' relative lack of marquee victories means they need to win at least one of their final two regular-season games to have a solid at-large case. The CBS Sports CFP Forecaster gives UCLA an 86.1% chance of making the field with a win over the Wolverines. A win would also lock up a spot in the Big Ten Championship Game for the Bruins, who close the regular season against crosstown rival USC next week. Can Wayne Knight break free?: Wayne Knight rattled off three straight 100-plus yard rushing performances during UCLA's first three Big Ten victories. But in the past five games, the James Madison transfer has eclipsed the century mark just once. Last week's 22-14 win over Illinois marked his first game this season without either a rushing or receiving touchdown. After averaging 253.2 rushing yards per game on 6.1 yards per attempt in their first five games, the Bruins have averaged just 152.2 yards per game on 4.1 yards per attempt over their last five. If there's one thing Michigan does reasonably well, it's defend the run. Opponents are averaging just 103.1 yards per game on the ground against the Wolverines. Ongoing quarterback battle: With two games left in the regular season, there still isn't an established starting quarterback at Michigan. It's been that kind of season for the Wolverines, who played both Bryce Underwood and Tommy Carr in last week's loss to Oregon. Interim offensive coordinator Jim Harding boiled this week's competition between the two signal-callers down to ball security. "Are you going to necessarily have an epiphany that in Week 11 the kid can do this particular thing?" Harding said. "I would not say that that's the case, but I think what you can evaluate in practice this week is who's valuing the importance of having the football at the end of the play. That honestly is the main piece in the evaluation is who can take care of the football." Hirschhorn In a universe where UCLA's offense fell apart after losing starting quarterback Nico Iamaleava and the team's sub-FBS transfers had minimal impact, Saturday's matchup in Ann Arbor would tilt a little differently. In previous years, such a battered version of the Bruins would have little hope of emerging victorious from the Big House, a place where they haven't won since 1982. However, the 2026 Wolverines don't exist in such a world. Instead, they have tried and failed to overcome issues under center all season, stymying an offense that probably doesn't have sufficient game-ready talent across the board. Meanwhile, the Bruins appear to have hit on former Cal Poly signal-caller Ty Dieffenbach, while James Madison transfer Wayne Knight has already racked up 15 touchdowns and over 1,000 yards from scrimmage. In many ways, UCLA looks like how Michigan did during its most recent successful period: tough and resilient with an ability to consistently perform above the program's perceived talent level. That reflects well on first-year Bruins head coach Bob Chesney, but it says plenty about the Wolverines' current headman as well. (Photo by Steven King/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Scotty White · SB Nation Thu, November 19, 2026 at 1:00 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Michigan football season felt over when the Wolverines lost to Michigan State, and that defeat seems to have had a similar impact on the team. Michigan lost on the road against Oregon, 31-7, last weekend, and it didn't look like anyone was mentally present for the Wolverines. This weekend presents a new challenge — the UCLA Bruins. UCLA is having a special season, especially considering this was one of the worst teams in the Big Ten last year. The Bruins are 10-0 and knocking on the doorstep of the Big Ten Championship and College Football Playoff. A win this weekend would clinch the Bruins a spot in Indy, and it would likely make it impossible for them to miss the CFP. Somehow, UCLA is only favored by 3.5 points leading up to this game. Does Vegas know something, or will it be another uninspiring performance from the Wolverines? Let's make some bold predictions for the game. Michigan will go to another backup QB The Oregon game was interesting, as Michigan went back-and-forth between Tommy Carr and Bryce Underwood, waiting for someone to provide a spark. The thing is, I really don't think it matters. I don't think the issue is with the quarterbacks at all, as I think Underwood and Carr have both shown some good flashes. I believe the real issue boils down to poor offensive line play and the refusal to involve the tight ends more. Still, the coaches are going to search for a spark. Brayden Fowler-Nicolosi, a transfer from Colorado State, should be next in line at the quarterback position. I'm honestly surprised we haven't seen him yet, but there's truly nothing to lose at this point. Give him a shot. Michigan gets shutout I don't like to reuse predictions in these, but I'm honestly shocked this hasn't happened yet and I feel like it's inevitable at this point. This offense has amazed us with levels of bad we didn't know existed, and I think it still has one more trick up its sleeve. UCLA is 10-0 in large part due to its defense. Remember, the Bruins have been without starting quarterback Nico Iamaleava since Oct. 10 when he got hurt at Oregon. Since then, only one team has hit 20 points against the Bruins. They are ranked No. 4 in the country in total defense. UCLA is shutting everyone down. Michigan barely avoided a shutout against Michigan State, a bad team with a bad defense. The Wolverines haven't been shutout at home since 1967, but that could change this weekend. UCLA wins, 17-0 UCLA is great defensively, but the Bruins have only eclipsed 30 points once with Ty Dieffenbach at quarterback, so I expect Michigan's defense to keep this one relatively close. Still, I just can't imagine the Wolverines finding any success offensively, and I would be shocked if UCLA doesn't easily cover the spread. Michigan's bowl hopes will hinge on The Game.

The football program's last title was the 1998 Pac-10 Championship, won in the regular season. Now, in just its third year as a Big Ten school, UCLA can go to the Big Ten Championship game with one more win in its last two games. Michigan is looking for anything positive at this point. The season crashed through the floor, going 2-5 in Big Ten play – losing to Oregon and Michigan State by a combined score of 46-13 – and now it needs a win in the last two games just to go to a bowl game. UCLA vs Michigan: Quick Hits Michigan closes with a bang: losing to Oregon 31-7 last week in Eugene, hosting UCLA this week, and finishing with the showdown against Ohio State in Columbus. UCLA closes at USC next week. It won't need the win if it can beat the Wolverines, but obviously, it's the rivalry game the Bruins want. The two teams haven't played since 2000, a 23-20 UCLA win. Starting in 1956 with a 42-13 win, UCLA is 8-3 in the series. How To Watch UCLA vs Michigan Date: Saturday, November 21, 2026 Game Time: 3:30 PM ET TV: CBS Location: Michigan Stadium, Ann Arbor, MI – Week 12 Schedule & Predictions – CFN Bowl & CFP Projections | Top 250 – CFN Week 12 Expert Picks Why UCLA Will Win Michigan doesn't do that whole scoring thing the kids are all into now. It was bad, there was a false ray of hope when Tommy Carr had a terrific day against a miserable Rutgers defense, and then everything got exponentially worse against Michigan State and Oregon. The Wolverines averaged 301 yards per game – 131st in the nation – and can't score even when they get into the red zone. But that's not the real problem. Michigan has turned it over multiple times in every game except for the wins over Oklahoma and Rutgers, and gave it away once in the loss to Iowa. It turned it over 13 times in the last six games. UCLA is No. 1 in the nation with 30 takeaways. Why Michigan Will Win UCLA isn't the type of team that wings the ball all over the yard. It's a tough, hard-nosed team, but it's not going to run away and hide with a big offensive explosion. The Bruins will play exactly the way Michigan wants. UCLA will need to run the ball, keep the tempo low, and rely on the lines – fine with the Wolverines. This is where the Wolverines can play it tough on the lines, work the field position battle, and try to keep this tight into the final few minutes. Despite the issues over the rough run, the defense is still among the ten best in America. UCLA vs Michigan Prediction, Betting Lines UCLA will have to work for it, but the defense will come up with the stop it needs late against the punchless Michigan offense. The Wolverines will come out fired up and cranked for the moment, marching down the field with a stunningly crisp opening scoring drive. But UCLA doesn't panic. The Bruin defense will be a rock on third downs, the offense will take the field goals and points when they're available, and Michigan's offense won't be able to take care of its opportunities to pull off the upset. Michigan enters as a 3.5-point underdog. Can it block out the mounting outside criticism and pull off an upset? Or will its struggles continue against a surging UCLA team? Here are our score predictions from MLive's beat writers: This was a game many of us had penciled in during the preseason as an automatic win for Michigan. First-year coach (Bob Chesney) and the Bruins having to make the cross-country trip to the mid-November cold in Michigan? It's almost the total opposite now, with UCLA unbeaten, ranked No. 4 in the country and favored to win by oddsmakers. The Bruins have an elite defense and strong run game, led by the Big Ten's best back in Wayne Knight, the ideal combination to pull this one out with backup quarterback Ty Dieffenbach expected to get the start. With JJ Buchanan out and Andrew Marsh's status in question, I'm expecting another difficult game for the Michigan offense. UCLA wins a low-scoring, grind-it-out affair in what should be an unseasonably warm afternoon in Ann Arbor. UCLA 17, Michigan 7 I get that traveling across three time zones is difficult for any team, but this spread still doesn't make much sense given Michigan's struggles and its injury situation. Whether or not Andrew Marsh plays Saturday, the Wolverines will face one of the country's best defenses without leading receiver JJ Buchanan and with a shorthanded offensive line. Oh, and Michigan still hasn't settled on a starting quarterback. That's not exactly a recipe for offensive success. Players and coaches have said this week that they're still motivated to make a bowl game, but their tone and the team's recent play suggest otherwise. Former Michigan receiver Semaj Morgan scores in his return to the Big House, while the Wolverines' offense sputters once again. UCLA 20, Michigan 10 The point spread is suspiciously small and maybe UCLA is overrated. I don't care. I'm not going to be fooled by Michigan again. If the Wolverines were going to show some fight recently they would have against their in-state rival or last week after their offensive coordinator was fired. Instead, they lost to Michigan State and Oregon, the latter in lopsided fashion. I made my prediction on the Wolverine Confidential podcast before we knew about Marsh, who is facing a misdemeanor charge of indecent exposure. If he doesn't play, it only elevates my confidence that Michigan's offense will struggle mightily. All those shutout stats we looked up during the Michigan State game, none of which were useful once Michigan scored late, will resurface Saturday. In this week's Roundtable, Maize n Brew staff members give some takeaways from last week's game at Oregon, offer up some bold predictions for tomorrow's game, and much more! As always, give us some of your thoughts/reactions from last week's game. Von : We can't just rag on how bad the offense was in this one, as the defense was also putrid and put up its worst performance of the year by a long shot. Michigan was out-gained, 326-140, at halftime, and 467-286 for the entire game. Dylan Raiola had 261 passing yards and three touchdowns in the first half alone. GOO! An all-around horrible performance, which is exactly what I expected going out west to play a legitimate team, especially after Kyle Whittingham ran his mouth about Oregon's NIL. Nick : I think things were going a bit better than expected actually with the defense able to keep it close for about the first 2.5-3 quarters of the game, but the dam finally broke and Oregon turned it into the blowout that most were expecting. I'm not upset with Jay Hill's group at all since they've been solid all year and have earned some slack. Regardless, this is all overshadowed by the fact Kyle Whittingham has become much too big a distraction in the second half of the season, and Saturday's loss was just the latest nail in the coffin on his tenure. Grace : I actually thought the team looked like it was giving a ton of effort, Oregon was just better. I'll be happy to root for these players no matter where they end up next season. Kellen : In a depressing way, it's actually impressive this offense is somehow getting worse week after week. Jason Beck is probably laughing on a comically large pile of cash like Scrooge McDuck after getting that buyout. Matt : Understandably, it feels as though the team has checked out. Outside of one Savion Hiter run, the offense performed as expected. However, the usually elite defense just didn't seem to play with any fire. The secondary was obliterated in a way we haven't seen this season, while the defensive line struggled to get any pressure on the quarterback. This type of game is exactly what happens when your season is already over by early November. Scotty : That game went about how I expected. The defense was worse than I thought it would be, but it's clear everyone isn't mentally in this season anymore, so I'm not very surprised by that. Charles : It was yet another embarrassment. Burn the tape and fire Kyle Whittingham. Where does this season rank among the most disappointing in Michigan football history, in your opinion? Von : In my lifetime, it's definitely up there. I don't think anything tops the embarrassment that was the 2014 season, but this is about as close as we're probably going to get given we currently have a bunch of coaches that don't care about/care to learn about the traditions of the program, and (some) players that turned on their coaches over a month ago and are probably patiently waiting for the transfer portal to open so they can get the hell out. I just imagine the players being like the old lady in Happy Gilmore — GET. ME. OUTTA. HERE! Nick : It's a lot to parse through 147 seasons of this program, but I'd say it's easily the most disappointing of my lifetime. Last season was bad at 9-3, but at least you could sell yourself on the team's youth and talent with Sherrone Moore being focused on anything but football. Whittingham was supposed to be able to keep things steady or elevate the program given all he'd done in the past, but instead, this season is not only spoiled, but there are real questions about the future, at least until he's inevitably (hopefully) replaced at the end of the year. Grace : It's one of the worst. When you start comparing stuff to Rich Rod's tenure, you know it's not good. Kellen : In terms of seasons I remember, this is right up there with the 3-9 2008 season under Rich Rod, the 5-7 season under Rich Rod in 2009, and the 5-7 2014 season under Brady Hoke. The same feeling of the players having no faith in the coaching staff just like the fanbase persists. I think those Rich Rod years were worse, but this is pretty damn close. Matt : I've been an avid fan since roughly 2003. I don't think it's hyperbolic to say this is No. 1 on the list in that timeframe. This isn't the worst Michigan team since 2003, as some of the Rich Rod and Brady Hoke teams were certainly worse. However, the gap between preseason expectations and on-field success has never been larger than 2026. Before the season, I thought the absolute floor for this team was 7-5. To already have five losses at this stage is downright shocking. Scotty : For me, it's No. 1. I really thought this was going to be a good year, and the talent was there for it to be. Wasted opportunity. Charles : It's certainly up there with the most disappointing seasons in school history. Since I started watching Michigan football in 2003, it's the most disappointing I've witnessed. The only seasons that compare are 2008, 2009 and 2014. I think all those teams were less talented than Michigan is this season, and losses to Minnesota and Michigan State have been truly inexplicable. In the end, it would be at least the most disappointing since 2008. The Wolverines are one win away from bowl eligibility…for the third week in a row. Does making a bowl game even matter? Does it mean anything for the young guys to get the extra practices? Von : No, the extra practices and the "game" itself would not matter one bit. If the Wolverines somehow win one of these next two games and becomes bowl eligible…why should the team even accept a bowl bid if Whittingham expects a ton of roster turnover this offseason? Whittingham has bashed his current players multiple times this year by saying he's excited to get the 2027 class (as well as a full portal class of his own) into the program. These current players have so much to play for these next two games, but a bowl game would be useless. Nick : I don't think at this point it really matters given much of this roster is going to look different next season. It seems like all parties would just like to get this season over with and I don't think this program has the Herculean effort in it it would take to win either of the next two games. Grace : No, making a bowl doesn't actually seem to make a difference. Beating Ohio State would feel nice, but that's because it's a rivalry game. I don't know getting to six or seven wins really moves the needle. Kellen : The extra practices would certainly help the young guys in theory, but as long as the current staff is in place, I'm not sure how much of a benefit those extra practices will be. Matt : I don't believe it matters. I wholeheartedly believe the Michigan program is going to have a mass exodus to the portal in roughly a week and a half. I also don't have the faith in at least the offensive coaching staff to develop the younger players. Scotty : Honestly, I just want this season to be over. Charles : I feel like I'm in the minority because I know bowl games don't really mean much in this day and age of college football, but I still love bowl games and think they are an overall positive for the program. Reaching a bowl game wouldn't make me change my mind on if Whittingham should return for another year because that ship has sailed, but I do think it would be a good thing for the program and players that opt to return. It's obviously been a pathetic season, but upsetting Ohio State or UCLA and playing in a bowl wouldn't hurt. Give us a bold prediction for tomorrow's game. Von : UCLA scores an offensive, defensive and special teams touchdown all in the same half. Nick : I think we'll see Savion Hiter build on his big game against Oregon and go more than 100 yards rushing again. He's one of the few spark plugs this offense has, so I'd like to see him heavily featured in this game. Grace : Michigan scores two touchdowns. Kellen : UCLA shuts out Michigan at home and Kyle Whittingham gets booed as he exits Michigan Stadium. Matt : Rod Moore gets in interception in his final game at Michigan Stadium. Scotty : I think I have to reuse the same one as last week because it just feels inevitable. Michigan will get shutout. It has to happen in one of the next two games. Charles : Michigan takes an early lead, then UCLA scores 21 unanswered points and runs away with a double-digit win. What's the final score and why? Von (5-5): UCLA 28, Michigan 7. Just bring on the Buckeyes already. Nick (4-4): UCLA should win, but I think this will look like a characteristic low-scoring defensive battle that we've seen from Michigan all year. Give me the Bruins 20-10. Grace (5-5): 28-14, UCLA. Because I can't pick Michigan every week in this terrible season. Kellen (6-4): UCLA wins, 27-0, because it actually has a competent football program. Matt : (6-2): UCLA 20 Michigan 3. Michigan's defense should be able to slow down UCLA's offense for a while, but the Michigan offense will be as feeble as ever. Scotty (2-4): UCLA wins, 17-0. I don't think the Bruins will do anything crazy offensively, but it won't take much scoring for them to earn an easy victory. Charles (4-3): I've given up on Michigan getting another win this season. If the Wolverines upset UCLA or Ohio State then so be it, but I can't bring myself to predict it. Give me UCLA, 21-10.
