away.headline: Blake Frazer, Rod Moore, Andrew Marsh Headline Michigan's Initial Injury Report vs. UCLA
away.blurb: We knew that JJ Buchanan was going to be out. Kyle Whittingham said so on Monday, but it's very concerning to see the likes of Andrew Marsh, and even Channing Goodwin to a certain extent on the list. Without Buchanan, Marsh is the certified alpha on the team and will be a key part of the Wolverines' passing attack — especially if there is any hope to get it going. And the offensive line remains a major issue. Blake Frazier is now officially out and the Wolverines played without him last weekend. Brady Norton is questionable, too, and the Wolverines could opt to play both Manuel Beigel and Marky Walbridge once again this weekend. After back-to-back losses to Michigan State and Oregon, the Wolverines are looking to get back in the win column. In fact, Michigan needs one more win in the last two weeks in order to go bowling. The Wolverines haven't missed a bowl game since 2014, the final year of Brady Hoke in Ann Arbor. If Michigan is going to gain bowl eligibility this weekend, the Wolverines are going to have to earn it. Michigan will host UCLA, which hasn't lost a game all year. The Bruins are one of the most surprising teams in college football. Despite losing Nico Iamaleava for the season, Bob Chesney has turned to his backup quarterback, but it's only resulted in success. If the Wolverines are going to beat UCLA , it's going to have to get the job done without a few players. Here's how Michigan's initial availability report looks heading into the Wolverines' Week 12 game against UCLA. More concern regarding the offense Michigan will also rely on Travis Johnson and Salesi Moa moving forward. Whittingham noted that tight end Mason Bonner could also see some play. It's also concerning to see Rod Moore on the list after he played last weekend against Oregon. The Wolverines' secondary got beat a few times against Oregon, and having a veteran back there like Moore would only help against UCLA. What’s at stake? UCLA football can break the program record for most wins in a single season if it can defeat Michigan and improve to 11-0. After Tuesday’s reveal of the third College Football Playoff rankings, UCLA remained at No. 4, meaning it has cushion to remain inside the coveted top 12. The Bruins control their destiny for a first-round bye in the CFP bracket and an appearance in the Big Ten championship game. Michigan is on the complete opposite side of the spectrum. Amid a 5-5 season, the program brought in Texas A&M athletic director Trev Alberts to replace Warde Manuel, who stepped down in July. With Alberts’ arrival, Coach Kyle Whittingham might be coaching for his job. Who’s better? If you told a UCLA fan during the DeShaun Foster era that the Bruins would be a healthy favorite at The Big House, they would think you’re insane. But here we are. UCLA runs the ball better than Michigan, in fact better than anyone in the Big Ten with 2,027 yards on the season. The Bruins’ passing attack has come through when it has needed to as quarterback Ty Dieffenbach threw for 232 yards and two touchdowns, including a crucial second-half drive, in defeating Illinois last week . And the defense is a world beater, ranking fourth in the nation in yards allowed per game (262.2) and first in forced turnovers (30). Michigan can’t land on a quarterback as it’s sifted through Bryce Underwood and Tommy Carr, hampered by both options’ woes. away.headline: UCLA football injury report: Jalen Woods, Riley Robell questionable for Michigan game
away.blurb: The first availability report of the week ahead of UCLA's Week 12 matchup at Michigan came out Wednesday. Two key UCLA players will be questionable for this week's game at Michigan. Both linebacker Jalen Woods and center Riley Robell are questionable to play this weekend, according to the initial Big Ten availability report that was released Wednesday. Woods got hurt midway through UCLA's win over Illinois last week and didn't return. UCLA got good news on Woods' MRI, Bob Chesney said Monday, but the injury was still significant enough for the linebacker to not return last week. Robell suffered a lower body injury against Minnesota two weeks ago, which kept him out last week and led the UCLA coaches to move guard Carter Sweazie to center. Additionally, starting right tackle Hall Schmidt , reserve wide receivers Jalen Saint Paul and Shane Rosenthal, reserve defensive linemen Ashton Sanders and reserve defensive end Ryan McCulloch have all been ruled out for the Michigan game. Michigan will be down its two starting offensive tackles against UCLA in Andrew Sprague and Blake Frazier. Additionally, key players Rod Moore (safety), Andrew Marsh (wide receiver), Brady Norton (offensive guard) and John Henry Daley (edge rusher) are all questionable. 247Sports Logo 247Sports 247Sports Home Transfer Portal Top FB Transfers FB Rec FB Rec FB Recruiting Home BK Rec BK Rec BK Recruiting Home Play Watch Watch CBS Sports College Football Forum Search Player Search Magnifying Glass Advanced player search Full site search Play Watch CBS Sports College Football Join NOVEMBER SALE! 50% off Annual VIP Membership to Bruin247 Join SALE! 50% Off Bruin247.com Annual VIP Membership today! The Tigers moved to 6-4 in Lane Kiffin's first season after losing a heartbreaker against Texas 22-21 last week. Tennessee has been steady since making a quarterback change to George MacIntyre , winning five of its last six games. The Volunteers pulled away from Texas A&M in a 22-7 victory, led by a dominant defensive performance in College Station. LSU and Tennessee have not played since 2022, a 40-13 dominant for the Volunteers in Baton Rouge. Before that, the Tigers won five straight dating back to 2006. This is the first trip back to Knoxville for Kiffin since the famous 31-26 Ole Miss win in 2021 that led to Kiffin being pelted by golf balls and mustard bottles. LSU vs. Tennessee: Need to know Bishop's rise: Tennessee running back DeSean Bishop turned down Power Four offers to walk on at his hometown program. Now, he's emerged as one of the best in the nation. The junior is rushing for 1,163 yards and 13 touchdowns to power the Volunteers, including 97 or more yards in six straight games. Disappointing debut: Kiffin was hired at LSU in one of the biggest coaching decisions of the past several years. In Year 1, the results have been decidedly mixed. The Tigers sit at a paltry 6-4, including 0-4 against CFP-ranked opponents. LSU could desperately use even a single meaningful victory to build some momentum heading into 2027. Passing game woes: Tennessee started the year with freshman Faizon Brandon before handing the keys to George MacIntyre, but neither has provided much dynamism. The Volunteers rank No. 123 nationally in passing offense, mustering only 7.1 yards per attempt. Making matters worse, top receiver Mike Matthews is likely out for the season with a knee injury suffered against Texas A&M. That's bad news going against LSU's strong passing defense. Neither quarterback has been consistent against great competition, and the defenses have shut down even elite opponents. Pete Fiutak · College Football News Thu, November 19, 2026 at 10:59 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Any thought that LSU was going to take the college football world by storm after Lane Kiffin took over ended with a tough 22-21 loss against Texas. It was the Tigers' fourth loss of the season, they're out of the College Football Playoff mix, and now it's time to play the spoiler role. Kiffin gets to play the villain, going back to his old coaching grounds – he was the Tennessee head coach in 2009 – and Tennessee will be fired up. The Vols are 8-2 after winning five of their last six games, and at No. 9 in the latest rankings, they're all but in the CFP if they win their last two games. LSU vs Tennessee: Quick Hits LSU closes out on the road at Arkansas after this. Lose to the Vols, and it'll be the third year in a row the program suffered a three-game losing streak. Tennessee goes to Vanderbilt to finish up the regular season. If it wins the final two games, it's in the mix for the SEC Championship along with the CFP. The two programs haven't met since 2022 – a 40-13 Tennessee win. LSU has won five of the last six, going back to 2005. How To Watch LSU vs Tennessee Date: Saturday, November 21, 2026 Game Time: 3:30 PM ET TV: ABC Location: Neyland Stadium, Knoxville, TN – Week 12 Schedule & Predictions – CFN Bowl & CFP Projections | Top 25 – CFN Week 12 Expert Picks Why LSU Will Win The talent is still there, the coaching is still great, and now the pressure is off. LSU isn't going anywhere this season, and now it can be Lane Unleashed as the team throws everything at a Vols team with all of the weight on its side of the field. The defense is the best in the SEC, the offense is the best in the SEC, the team holds the ball longer than anyone else in the conference, and no one in America generates more sacks. Tennessee has a problem keeping defenses out of the backfield, and now, here come the Tigers. Why Tennessee Will Win LSU might generate the most sacks in America, but Tennessee can bring the heat, too – the Tigers are No. 2 in sacks. It didn't sack Marcel Reed in last week's 22-7 win over Texas A&M, but it gave him a rough time. Now the Vols are back at home, where they take their defensive production up several notches. The defense has allowed just one touchdown pass in five games in Neyland, but in this, it's about the Tennessee run defense. LSU is 1-3 when running for fewer than 140 yards. Auburn and Furman – the Vols called off the dogs against the Paladins – are the only teams to hit the 140-yard mark. LSU vs Tennessee Prediction, Betting Lines Here's the thing about LSU this season. It pounces on the weak, but its best win is … at Auburn? That's good, but there really isn't a second-best victory going 0-4 against the current CFP-ranked teams on the slate. Tennessee is a top team. This might not be the sexiest team going, but it's got grit. It's a tough defensive team that doesn't make a ton of mistakes, and it doesn't get rattled. LSU will be terrific, but like the Kentucky and Texas games, it'll crumble late in the final moments. picks.headline: ESPN model issues bizarre prediction for LSU-Tennessee game
picks.blurb: ESPN model issues bizarre prediction for LSU-Tennessee game - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football CFP And Bowl Games James Harden drops 51 in Cavs’ NBA Cup win over Pacers TRENDING Maye reportedly fractures fibula Report: Dodgers get Royce Lewis Kane to miss multiple months Puka Nacua suspended 'GTA 6' impacts sports ESPN model issues bizarre prediction for LSU-Tennessee game Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads LSU and Tennessee look to be pretty evenly matched heading into Saturday's Week 12 college football action. Very evenly matched. That's according to the College Football Power Index prediction model, a computer system devised by ESPN analysts to project how teams will perform in the future. Looking over what LSU and Tennessee can put on the field , and after simulating the game 20,000 times, even they could hardly come to a conclusion. A prediction that raises eyebrows Tigers Head Coach Lane Kiffin, The LSU Tigers take on Alabama. November 7, 2026; Baton Rouge, LA, USA; at Tiger Stadium. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) ESPN's model is picking the Tigers to win by exactly zero points. Yes, zero. The seemingly contradictory projection has turned some heads, particularly with Tennessee entering the matchup as the No. 9 ranked team in the country. A zero-point margin essentially suggests the model views the SEC rivals as dead even, making the Tigers' projected victory more of a technical distinction than a meaningful advantage. Tennessee has much more at stake While LSU's season, and Lane Kiffin's debut, are just about over, Tennessee has plenty on the line this weekend. The Vols' No. 9 ranking puts them inside the College Football Playoff bracket as of this week. But it's a low-enough position that they could jeopardize everything with a mistake late in the season. More: Predicting SEC football scores for Week 12's biggest games For LSU, pulling off a road victory against a nationally ranked opponent would represent at least a late-season high for Kiffin in his debut season. The numbers tell a different story Sep 12, 2026; Atlanta, Georgia, USA; Tennessee Volunteers running back DeSean Bishop (18) celebrates after a touchdown run against the Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets in the fourth quarter at Bobby Dodd Stadium at Hyundai Field. Mandatory Credit: Brett Davis-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) The prediction becomes more interesting when examining the underlying numbers. According to ESPN's matchup predictor, LSU has a 50.1 percent chance of winning, compared with Tennessee's 49.9 percent. That's essentially a statistical coin flip. However, the teams arrive with contrasting strengths. LSU averages 490.3 yards of total offense per game, ranking eighth nationally. Tennessee, meanwhile, allows just 14.3 points per game, the seventh-best scoring defense in the country. The Volunteers also rank eighth nationally in passing defense, surrendering only 164.2 yards per contest. And they're one of the best rushing teams in the country, ranking 13th with 214 yards per game. More: SEC power rankings entering college football Week 12 Can LSU pull off the upset? There is a reason ESPN's projection deserves attention. LSU's offense has demonstrated considerable firepower at times, and the Tigers have been competitive despite their 6-4 record. Three of their four losses have come by a combined six points. Still, Tennessee enters at 8-2 and has been particularly impressive at Neyland Stadium, outscoring opponents 199-68 at home this season. The takeaway? ESPN is effectively calling this matchup a toss-up, not predicting a literal scoreless-margin victory. With LSU's explosive offense facing Tennessee's formidable defense, Saturday's showdown could deliver an intriguing SEC battle.

Tennessee's College Football Playoff hopes are on the line this weekend against LSU. If the Vols beat LSU on Saturday in Neyland Stadium, they'll just need a win in the regular-season finale against Vanderbilt to lock down a spot in the College Football Playoff. But if Tennessee loses to LSU, they can likely kiss their playoff hopes goodbye. LSU, which has four losses, is out of the playoff picture. The Tigers' 6-4 record, however, isn't indicative of how good of a team they are. LSU has arguably the most talented roster in the nation, and they are just a couple of plays away from being 8-2. Tennessee has a 59% chance to make the College Football Playoff and a 4% chance to win the national title, according to the A to Z Sports CFB Playoff Predictor (updated November 15, 2026). Combine that with the fact that Tennessee will be without several key players against the Tigers — specifically left guard Nic Moore and wide receiver Mike Matthews — and it's easy to see why there's some concern about this game on Rocky Top. Former Georgia QB Aaron Murray makes his prediction for LSU vs Tennessee Former Georgia quarterback Aaron Murray predicted last week that Tennessee would beat Texas A&M by 13 points last week (the Vols won by 15 points), but he's not making the same kind of prediction for the LSU game. Murray has the Tigers taking down the Vols on Saturday, predicting that LSU will leave Neyland Stadium with a 23-17 win. One of the main reasons Murray is predicting an LSU win is because the Vols will be without Mike Matthews. "This (LSU) defense is going to be able to put you in third-and-long situations," said Murray. "And they're going to be able to get to the quarterback with Princewill Umanmielen and Jordan Ross coming off the edge. "… Can Tennessee's offense, without Matthews and with a banged up quarterback — it's possibly Faizon Brandon back in there playing quarterback — get the job done against LSU in this matchup? I don't feel very confident. Which is why I'm going with LSU 23-17 in this football game. If Mike Matthews was healthy, and if [George MacIntyre] — I don't know what the knee is right now, maybe he's 100 percent for the game [and I would feel different]. But still, no Mike Matthews. I think that's a big problem for the Tennessee Volunteers. So I think LSU wins the game." I think that's a fair prediction from Murray. There are certainly questions about the Vols' offense without Matthews. The junior wide receiver was easily Tennessee's most dynamic playmaker. But LSU has failed to finish games in the fourth quarter this season and that's an area where Tennessee has thrived. If the Vols can get this game to the fourth quarter, I like their chances. But if they get to the fourth quarter and they're down multiple scores, it could be too big of a hill for Tennessee's offense to climb. This article was originally published on A to Z Sports. After being listed as questionable every day leading in to their game against Texas, Whit Weeks is listed as doubtful this week. He dressed out fully and participated in warmups, but did not play a snap. Matt Zenitz of CBS Sports has reported that not only is the senior linebacker expected to miss Saturday’s contest, but it’s looking more likely that he’s done for the season. The other notable news for LSU is wide receivers Jackson Harris and Winnie Watkins being listed as questionable. We’ve seen Harris come up hobbled a few times over the past few games, but he’s shown grit and toughness and returns to the field. It is unclear what his specific injury is. Jhase Thomas being listed as probable likely means that he is expected to play, but did not practice fully on Wednesday. As for Tennessee, they have 10 players listed as out. The big news, though, is that quarterback George MacIntyre is not listed. He left their game last weekend against Texas A&M in the 3rd quarter with a knee injury and did not return. After taking over for Faizon Brandon as the Volunteers starting QB, MacIntyre is 4-1 and has helped them reach the top-10 in the College Football Playoff rankings. Tennessee comes in to Saturday’s contest ranked #9 and 8-2, while LSU fell out of the rankings following last week’s last second loss to Texas that dropped them to 6-4. picks.blurb: Game Preview as SMU Travels to Face No. 5 Notre Dame in Tough Road Test Skip to main content SI.COM MEN'S BASKETBALL WOMEN'S BASKETBALL SMU SPORTS NEWS FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS 2025 FOOTBALL BRACKET SI.COM MUSTANGS FB MEN'S BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM MISTANGS BB DALLAS — The SMU Mustangs (7-3, 5-3 ACC) face one of their toughest road trips of the season this weekend. The Mustangs will travel to South Bend to face the No. 5 Notre Dame Fighting Irish (9-1) Saturday night at the historic Notre Dame Stadium. The Mustangs haven’t traveled to South Bend since the late 1980s. SMU holds a 1-6 record against the Fighting Irish on the road. Notre Dame leads the all-time series 10-3 overall. SMU faces a tall task after being routed in their first ACC loss at Gerald J. Ford Stadium in over three years. The Mustangs were drilled by No. 13 Wake Forest 49-7 last week. The Demon Deacons outgained SMU 535-275 while holding the Mustangs to 209 passing yards and 69 total rushing yards. As a result, SMU's chances of heading to Charlotte for the ACC championship game and a potential shot at the College Football Playoff have grown slimmer. SMU Head Football Coach Rhett Lashlee spoke during this week's media availability on his team’s performance last week and the challenge that this week presented to bounce back. “Life’s about opportunities, we had one last week we didn't take advantage of it. We have done a good job of taking advantage of our opportunities here. We did not put our best foot forward last week,” said Lashlee during Tuesday’s media availability. “Sometimes when that happens if we were playing someone that we were expected to beat or what not. I don’t know what you gain from that, but having the opportunity to go on the road against an elite opponent we know it's going to take our very best to beat regardless of what happened last week. I like that it's a great opportunity, a great challenge, and we get to see what we are made of and how we respond to that opportunity.” Notre Dame has been a top team in college football this season. After famously being left out of the College Football Playoff last season, Head Football Coach Marcus Freeman and his team have gone to work to ensure the Fighting Irish don’t leave any boxes unchecked for a guaranteed ticket to the postseason. The Irish are 9-1 through 10 games with a staple win over the ACC leader and former No. 1 team in the country, the Miami Hurricanes, atop their season resume. Notre Dame leads the nation in the fewest yards allowed to opposing offenses. While boasting one of the nation's best offenses. Junior quarterback C.J. Carr is top 10 in passing touchdowns this season with 23, while being among the top 25 in total passing yards with 2,385 this season. Carr has been in the Heisman conversation all season in his second season as a starter. He has only been intercepted twice and sacked three times this season. He is coming off a 200-yard performance against Boston College, after throwing for a season-high 319 yards against Miami. The second-year starter has a veteran pair of wide receivers bolstering the passing attack. Senior wide receiver Jordan Faison leads the receiver room with 615 yards on 49 catches with six scores. Not far behind him is junior receiver Micah Gilbert, who has recorded 614 yards on 38 grabs with six of his own scores this season. Fellow senior Jaden Greathouse is also a reliable weapon for Carr this year, securing 25 catches for 354 yards after dealing with injury for most of last season. The multiple weapons for the home team will be a massive test on the SMU’s secondary. Pick your champion (you can change it later). We’ll email you when brackets open. After losing both star running backs to the NFL, Notre Dame’s rushing attack has been bolstered by a pair of young stars with only 11 yards separating them. Freshman running back Jonaz Walton leads the team in rushing yards with 655 yards this season, averaging 7.0 yards per carry this season with five scores. The true freshman ran for over 140 yards and a score in Notre Dame’s 41-7 win over Boston College last week. Sophomore running back Nolan James Jr. is second on the team in rushing yards with 644. The second year back has had more than 120 attempts running the football this season, with a knack for finding the end zone. James Jr. has scored 10 times so far this season, the most on the roster. SMU allowed 286 rushing yards with 6.4 yards per carry against Wake Forest last week. The Mustangs will have one of the most talented backfield duos in the country rushing at them Saturday night. Lashlee went on to describe Notre Dame’s style of play as methodical and patient, yet still able to be explosive. “The way they play allows them to be patient, methodical, and just wear on you,” said Lashlee. “Because of their talent they create explosive plays, but they are not necessarily wired where they have to. They have no problem going on 10, 12, 13 play drives and just wearing on you. So that's what you worry about over the course of the game.” SMU gears up for one of its toughest tests of the season Saturday in a game that has been circled on the calendar since the schedule was released. It doesn't matter – as long as the Irish win, they'll end up in the tournament. But drop a game over the last two weeks, and all CFP bets are off. SMU had its chance last week to all but land a spot in the ACC Championship, but one 49-7 rocking from Wake Forest later, and now it's looking to play spoiler to Notre Dame's season. Notre Dame vs SMU: Quick Hits SMU not only got blown out by Wake Forest, but that was the final home game. The Mustangs close out at Stanford. Notre Dame still has to deal with a road game at Syracuse to close things out. These two haven't played since 1989 – a 59-6 Notre Dame win. The Irish are 10-3 in the series going back to 1930. How To Watch Notre Dame vs SMU Date: Saturday, November 21, 2026 Game Time: 7:30 PM ET TV: NBC Location: Notre Dame Stadium, Notre Dame, IN – Week 12 Schedule & Predictions – CFN Bowl & CFP Projections | Top 25 – CFN Week 12 Expert Picks Why SMU Will Win SMU is still a dangerous team, even after the disaster against the Demon Deacons. The offense is terrific, with a great pace and balance that can be impossible to stop when it gets into a rhythm. Notre Dame hasn't faced too many sharp passing teams, but there was a problem against the stronger quarterbacks. BYU's Bear Bachmeier hit 65% of his passes in the 28-24 win, and Miami's Darian Mensah almost pulled the game out of the fire, throwing for 269 yards and three scores. One loss, one close call, and those were the two times the Irish allowed more than 300 total yards. SMU has one of the nation's most efficient passing games for an offense that averages 456 yards per game. Why Notre Dame Will Win How did Wake Forest destroy SMU? It came out roaring, and it was over. The Demon Deacons cranked up the pass rush against a leaky SMU line, and the three takeaways made things ugly. Yes, SMU works with a pace, but when it doesn't work, everything fizzes. But it's about the takeaways. SMU is 2-3 when turning it over multiple times, with 14 turnovers packed into those five games, and with nine turnovers in the three road games. Notre Dame is sixth in the nation in takeaways with 20. Notre Dame vs SMU Prediction, Betting Lines Yes, the Mustangs have a fun offense, and the quick-hitting style will hit the Irish defense for a few scores to throw a scare into the fan base for a half, but CJ Carr and the Notre Dame passing game are pretty good, too. Between the turnovers and lots of penalties, SMU isn't perfect. A few good drives will stall with giveaways, and even though the pass rush will get to Carr on a few third downs, the Irish will be locked in. They'll take over and pull away in the second half. picks.blurb: Notre Dame vs SMU Game Predictions - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football CFP And Bowl Games James Harden drops 51 in Cavs’ NBA Cup win over Pacers TRENDING Maye reportedly fractures fibula Report: Dodgers get Royce Lewis Kane to miss multiple months Puka Nacua suspended 'GTA 6' impacts sports Story by Roundtable Sports Notre Dame vs SMU Game Predictions (Angela Driskell, Irish Breakdown) Bryan Driskell · Roundtable Sports Fri, November 20, 2026 at 2:00 PM UTC · 7 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Notre Dame will look to build its College Football Playoff resume when it takes on the 7-3 SMU Mustangs. The Irish fell to 6th in the playoff rankings on Tuesday despite blowing out Boston College by a 41-7 score last weekend. Notre Dame doesn't have a ranked opponent left on the schedule, but the Mustangs will help improve the overall strength of schedule, should the Irish earn a win. Notre Dame makes the playoff if they win out, but a dominant win would be even more helpful. Location : Notre Dame Stadium (Notre Dame, Ind.) Date : Saturday - November 21 Time : 7:30 PM ET Networ k: NBC/Peacock Here are our staff predictions for the game: Prediction : Notre Dame 38, SMU 17 Some of the magnitude of this game was diminished when SMU lost to Wake Forest last weekend in a blowout (49-7). SMU is a much better football team than it showed against the Demon Deacons, and that game reminded me a lot of Notre Dame's loss to Miami in 2017. It was one of those games that just got away from them early, but make no mistake, SMU is a dangerous football team. Notre Dame will need to play at a high level, because I expect SMU to come out looking to make an early statement and bounce back from their bad loss last weekend. The key for Notre Dame will be coming out early and jumping all over the Mustangs. They will need to quickly take away SMU's confidence and not let their potent offense get into any kind of rhythm. That will require the defense to be turned loose and be allowed to attack quarterback Kevin Jennings . If they are allowed to do that, and if the DL handles business, they will force Jennings to make mistakes, and that's how Notre Dame rolls in this game. My prediction is based on SMU being able to make some plays early due to their impressive talent at wide receiver and the fact Jennings is a dangerous player. I expect the Irish defense to quickly get up to speed and slow SMU down over the final two quarters. On the other side of the ball, Notre Dame will look to establish the run game early and get Nolan James Jr . and Jonaz Walton to get going. They will look to soften the Mustangs up and that's when CJ Carr should get rolling and pick the Mustangs apart. If the offensive line handles business the Notre Dame offense should have a big day and the Irish should roll. If Carr gets going early the offense could be extremely difficult to stop in this matchup. Prediction : Notre Dame 41, SMU 13 This is the final of three major tests for the 6th ranked Notre Dame Fighting Irish. SMU is coming off a 49-7 loss to Wake Forest at home during their own Senior Day matchup, but don't let that fool you, this is still a talented team making the trip up north. But like a lot of their opponents for the 2026 season, this matchup is more about Notre Dame living up to its potential than it is about facing an opponent that's superior. As it was said best in Wednesday's show, Marcus Freeman needs to know 'what time it is' in college football. SMU is a quality opponent, but not good enough that simply winning the game will boost their resume all on its own. I expect the Fighting Irish offense to come out firing early. Quarterback CJ Carr will hit some big plays early. The biggest question, will Notre Dame keep their foot on the gas after jumping out to an early lead? I think they answer that to a degree, but Freeman needs to learn from the lessons he's experienced in the previous two seasons. I have the Irish winning by 28 on Senior Day. I'm picking Notre Dame to win convincingly against SMU, but this game is about more than simply adding another win to the schedule. With the College Football Playoff committee evaluating every result, the Irish need to make a statement and show that they belong among the nation's elite. Notre Dame cannot afford to play down to its competition or let SMU hang around into the second half. This is an opportunity to dominate on both sides of the football, establish the running game, stretch the field offensively, and demonstrate the kind of physical superiority that separates playoff contenders from everyone else. The Irish need to take care of business, but they also need to make it look impressive. SMU has enough offensive talent, particularly with quarterback Kevin Jennings , to make things interesting if Notre Dame allows it. However, coming off a 49-7 loss to Wake Forest, the Mustangs are vulnerable, and Notre Dame needs to take full advantage. I want to see the Irish defense create turnovers, get after Jennings, and keep SMU from finding any offensive rhythm. More importantly, Notre Dame needs to keep its foot on the gas rather than become conservative with a comfortable lead. The committee won't just see another win but it will see how the Irish perform against an opponent they are expected to handle. This is a chance to deliver a dominant performance, build momentum, and send a message that Notre Dame is a legitimate national championship contender. Prediction : Notre Dame 52, SMU 13 Before last weekend, I was going to pick a closer game (something like 38-24), but a combination of both the SMU blowout loss to Wake Forest and Notre Dame's dominant win over Boston College made me reconsider. First, I was pleased that the Irish played the attacking style of defense against Boston College that we saw for the second half of 2025, early in 2026, and then again against Miami. I don't think SMU's offensive line can hold up against the Irish front-seven when they play aggressively. The Mustangs gave up three sacks and six tackles for loss to Wake Forest, and rank 96th in the country in sacks allowed in road games this season. Getting SMU behind the sticks is going to put the onus on Kevin Jennings to make plays. He is really talented, but has a penchant for putting the ball in danger and making a few of those "what is he doing" kind of plays per game. There's a reason that SMU ranks 118th in the country in turnover margin at -6, and Notre Dame ranks 2nd at +16. Also, whether its due to corruption, malice, or just plain incompetence, there are no guarantees for Notre Dame when it comes to the CFP Committee. Marcus Freeman knows that it's not enough to just win these final two games - the Irish need to be dominant if they want to secure a home playoff game. With Wake Forest having such a big win last weekend over SMU - in Dallas no less - I think that will force Freeman and the Irish to keep the pedal down more than would be typical on a Senior Day when the staff typically tries to get all seniors a couple snaps once the game is in hand. Notre Dame's offense should not have much trouble moving the ball against a Mustangs defense that was blitzed by the two best offenses it faced (giving up 488.5 YPG against ranked opponents), and I think the Irish send a message on the scoreboard. Prediction : Notre Dame 35, SMU 10 SMU is a rising program, no question, which was why I was definitely surprised to tune into the game in the second half on Saturday to see such a lopsided score against Wake Forest. The Demon Deacons hammered SMU, leaving them off the scoreboard in the first half and quickly lighting up the scoreboard. While the Mustangs can certainly compete with anybody and Saturday's score was definitely out of character with how their season has gone, I don't think Notre Dame will have much trouble with them, provided they get off to a good start and play disciplined football. It really feels like Mike Denbrock has found his groove, with a great mix of run-and-pass with CJ Carr and Notre Dame's three-headed monster in the backfield: Jonaz Walton , Nolan James Jr. and Aneyas Williams . Give me the Irish.

home.headline: Notre Dame football's top run-stuffer set to return vs. SMU
home.blurb: The 6-foot-1, 285-pound Pittsburgh transfer had been listed as questionable on the official injury report since going down seven snaps into the Navy game on Oct. 31 in Foxborough, MA. Fellow defensive tackle Jason Onye, injured five snaps into the Navy game, remains questionable with a right knee injury as of Thursday’s late-week availability update. Partridge recruited Brewu to Pitt out of Westerville, OH before spending the 2024-25 seasons with the Indianapolis Colts. The reunion has been good for both parties. “We made sure and pointed it out (in film study),” Partridge said of Brewu’s advanced technique against Navy. “That's just an example of how he's playing the game right now. I’m proud of him. I’m happy for him.” “(Brewu) has played really, really well,” defensive line coach Charlie Partridge said in early November. “I'm proud of his growth. He's had a lot to learn since he's been here. It's a completely different style of defense than Pittsburgh plays, and it was a challenge for him early. “ Brewu averaged 24 defensive snaps through the first seven games, peaking at 35 snaps in the Oct. 17 loss at BYU. His 84.3 overall defensive grade, per Pro Football Focus, is tied for eighth among FBS defensive tackles with at least 175 snaps this season. His 84.5 grade as a run stuffer is seventh. Oregon transfer Tionne Gray (70.1) is tied for 139th overall at defensive tackle, while Armel Mukam (69.1) is tied for 161st. “Because I've known him so long, I was probably harder on him than some of the other guys,” Partridge said. “But I was that way because I want him to be the best version of himself. And to his credit, he weathered that storm and was playing really good football (before the injury).” Brewu averaged 37 defensive snaps across 13 games in 2025 at Pitt with a high of 61 in Week 3 at West Virginia. His overall PFF grade was 78.4, tying him for 17th among the 147 defensive tackles with at least 450 games snaps last year. “He's rushing the passer well, he's playing the run well,” Partridge said. “There was a play against Navy where it was beautiful. He played the cut (block) with two hands, he cleared the cut, and he leapt off the ground to tackle the guy from behind. Not many people are going to put that on their bingo card to say, ‘I'm going to put this on Instagram.’“ Brewu is tied for third on the team with two sacks, and he counts three tackles for loss among his 16 total tackles. Like Kentucky, Missouri has lost its past two games, but the Tigers scored more points in losses to Texas and Georgia than the Wildcats did in losses to Tennessee and Florida. Missouri has been held to fewer than 20 points just once this season while Kentucky has scored more than 21 points just once in its past four games. Can Kentucky's offense match Missouri? Here is what you need to know heading into the 7:30 p.m. game . What is at stake for Kentucky football at Missouri The losses to Tennessee or Florida essentially ended Kentucky's College Football Playoff hopes, but The Athletic's model still gives Kentucky a 7% chance to make the field. The model projects that chance would jump to 20% with a win in Columbia. Even if Kentucky wins its final two games, it still needs help in the form of losses from at least four of BYU, Wake Forest, Texas Tech, Oregon, Ohio State and Iowa. All Kentucky can control is its own performance, though. Even if Kentucky does return to the playoff hunt, beating Missouri would be big for the program. Kentucky has only won six SEC games in a season once previously (1977). It has not won four road games in a season since 1984. It has not won four SEC road games since 1977. Finishing at 6-3 in SEC play would give Kentucky a leg up in the pecking order for the Citrus Bowl, which has the first pick of SEC teams after the playoff is filled. A Citrus Bowl appearance versus a traditional Big Ten power would be a nice consolation prize for missing the playoff. Kentucky football injury report Backup linebacker Alex Afari was an unexpected addition to the "out" list on Wednesday's SEC availability report. Nickel back Jaden Smith (ACL) is out for the season. Backup linebacker Antwan Smith (ankle) might be back for the bowl game but is not expected to return in the regular season. Linebacker Quintavion Norman, who primarily contributes on special teams, is also out this week. Cornerback Grant Grayton, who has missed the past eight games with an injury, is listed as doubtful. Even if he does not play this week, that is a sign he is nearing a return. Wide receiver Nic Anderson, who has missed two of the past three games, was listed as questionable. Kentucky vs. Missouri prediction Kentucky has played well on the road this season outside of the fourth quarter at Tennessee, so the environment should not be a concern. The recent offensive production is, though. On paper, UK might not have enough firepower to knock off a Missouri team with the second-leading rusher in the SEC (Jamal Roberts) and fourth-leading passer (Austin Simmons). Missouri 28, Kentucky 21. The final word "There is a ton to play for. This is an opportunity to get our sixth win in the SEC, to go 8-3, to redefine who we are as a program. We've created the standard and expectations of winning because of what we did the last 10 games. That's where I want this to be. That's what I want our expectations to be as a program: is that we are supposed to win every single game that we play. Just like our fans, I want them to think we should win every single game, because we have proven that we can go do it." – Will Stein Missouri quarterback Austin Simmons (13) is the SEC’s fourth-leading passer, and Tigers running back Jamal Roberts (left) is the league’s second-leading rusher entering Saturday’s game against Kentucky. picks.headline: Missouri Defense Preview: Can Kentucky's offense bounce back?
picks.blurb: Missouri Defense Preview: Can Kentucky's offense bounce back? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football CFP And Bowl Games James Harden drops 51 in Cavs’ NBA Cup win over Pacers TRENDING Maye reportedly fractures fibula Report: Dodgers get Royce Lewis Kane to miss multiple months Puka Nacua suspended 'GTA 6' impacts sports Story by Wildcats Wire Missouri Defense Preview: Can Kentucky's offense bounce back? Braxton Howard, UK Wildcats Wire · Wildcats Wire Thu, November 19, 2026 at 1:25 AM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Kentucky football travels to CoMo for the final road game of the season against the Missouri Tigers. The Wildcats offense desperately needs to respond after scoring just 20 points in the last two weeks which has led to back-to-back losses. Missouri is a well coached, good all around football team and the defense has been consistent this season. However, the Tigers had their worst defensive performance of the season on the road last week against Georgia. Both teams are coming off back-to-back losses, Kentucky has scored just 20 points on offense in the past two weeks. Conversely, the Missouri defense has allowed 72 points over the last two weeks, albeit to Georgia and Texas. Kentucky has to find some of the offensive success they had before the bye week if they want to finish the season on a strong note. A win at Missouri would give the Wildcats six wins in SEC play, which has only happened once in program history and that was in the 1977 season. I fully expect a motivated performance from both teams to try and put an end to their respective two-game losing streaks. Kentucky's offensive line was named a semifinalist for the Joe Moore Award and have since had to of their worst performances of the season. Last week against Florida was the worst the offensive line has looked all season, so you can almost guarantee they will respond the right way in this game. Quiet frankly, they have to because if the offensive line plays like they did against the Gators they will be in danger of a winless month of November. Missouri's defense has playmakers at every level, but they will allow teams to move the football. Among SEC teams, the Tigers rank 10th in success rate allowed, 7th in pass success rate allowed and 12th in rush success rate allowed. Missouri also ranks 8th in the SEC in EPA/play allowed, 7th in EPA/pass allowed and 12th in EPA/rush allowed. The Tigers have also allowed explosive plays this season, as they rank 14th in the conference in explosive play rate allowed. This will be a difficult matchup for Kentucky, but it starts by winning the line of scrimmage and getting the run game going. The Wildcats averaged just two yards per carry against Florida and had just 61 rushing yards. They will lose this game if they can not turn that around, but the Missouri run defense has struggled at times this season. Kentucky has to stay ahead of the chains and that starts with the run game on early downs, which is something they had been good at all season. We mentioned the Tigers have playmakers at every level of the defense, and that starts up front with edge defender Daeden Hopkins. Hopkins leads the team in sacks (7) and tackles for loss (7.5). Linebacker Nicholas Rodriguez leads the middle of the defense, Rodriguez is a tackling machine with a team-leading 107 tackles on the season; he also has seven tackles for loss and 3.5 sacks on the year. The secondary is led by safety Santana Banner, Banner has 84 tackles on the season, 6 pass breakups and 2.5 tackles for loss. Kentucky has to account for these three players, as they are the strength of this Missouri defense at every level. Hopkins, Rodriguez and Banner have each forced two fumbles this season as well. They have consistently made big time plays for the Tigers all season long. Kentucky has to find ways to exploit this defense and avoid letting these three players make game changing plays. In a lot of ways, this matchup is about Kentucky after scoring just 20 points in the last eight quarters. The offense just is not playing well, and what happened on the line of scrimmage against Florida was alarming. Kentucky has to get the big blue wall back to playing like semifinalists for the Joe Moore Award. This offense lacks explosive plays and yards after contact ability, so they will continue to struggle if the offensive line can't get back to playing at a high level. picks.headline: BY THE NUMBERS: Previewing Kentucky vs. Missouri
Kentucky vs. Missouri game glance, opening odds, and early prediction
picks.blurb: Kentucky vs. Missouri game glance, opening odds, and early prediction | A Sea Of Blue Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo A Kentucky Wildcats Community A Sea Of Blue November 21, 2026 A Sea Of Blue Notifications Notifications The Feed Sections Kentucky Wildcats Basketball College Basketball Recruiting Kentucky Wildcats Football College Football Recruiting Betting Betting News FanDuel College Football Odds FanDuel College Basketball Odds Kentucky Football Odds Kentucky Basketball Odds College Football Picks and Predictions College Basketball Picks and Predictions Library Community Guidelines Media Resources Login / Sign Up Search The Feed Sections Expand Kentucky Wildcats Basketball Betting Expand Betting News Library Expand Community Guidelines Community Guidelines All communities Notifications Kentucky Wildcats Football Can the Cats get back on track? Nine days ago, Kentucky Football was in the College Football Playoff conversation. Now, the Wildcats are trying to save a season that was turning into something special. The 21-14 loss to Florida on Saturday night at Kroger Field hurt more than most. Kentucky came in as a three-point favorite at home against a 5-4 Gators team. The Cats took a 7-2 lead into halftime and still led 14-13 going into the fourth quarter. Then Florida took over. Aaron Philo ran for 102 yards, the Gators ran for 211 as a team, and Kentucky managed just 61 rushing yards on 27 carries. That’s a season low for a team that came in averaging almost 164 per game. Will Stein didn’t sugarcoat it afterward. He said his team came up short in all three phases. That one stings because of how good this season had been. This was the team that went to College Station and beat No. 9 Texas A&M by 10. It came back from 17 down to win in overtime at South Carolina, beat No. 10 LSU 35-34 in overtime and sent the fans onto the field, then won in Norman. Kentucky was 7-1 and ranked in the top ten of the CFP rankings. Back-to-back losses to Tennessee and Florida later, the playoff dream is just about gone. But there’s still a lot to play for. Kentucky is 7-3 and bowl eligible with two games left: at Missouri and Louisville at home. Win both, then win a bowl game, and Kentucky reaches 10 wins. The program has only done that four times in its history: 1950, 1977, 2018 and 2021. In Stein’s first year, against what his own players called a whole lot of doubt back in August, that would be a remarkable finish. It starts Saturday night in Columbia. Matchup: Kentucky (7-3) at Missouri (6-4, 3-4 SEC) When: Saturday, Nov. 21, 7:30 p.m. ET Where: Faurot Field at Memorial Stadium, Columbia, MO. TV: SEC Network Odds: Missouri -6.5, over/under 50.5 (FanDuel) All-time series: Kentucky leads 9-5 Last meeting: Missouri won 38-21 in Lexington in 2023 Opponent at a Glance: Missouri Tigers Head coach: Eli Drinkwitz (7th season) Missouri started the year ranked No. 25 in the preseason polls. For a while, it looked like the Tigers were exactly who people thought they were. They blew out Florida 45-17, held Texas A&M to six points in a 27-6 win and beat Arkansas by 24. The problem is what happened against good teams. Missouri lost at Mississippi State in September, lost 31-3 at Ole Miss, lost 34-20 at home to Texas and just got rolled 48-21 by No. 1 Georgia in Athens. Two straight losses ended the Tigers’ playoff hopes. The Georgia game was ugly from the first snap. Quarterback Austin Simmons threw an interception on the first play, Georgia scored two plays later, and Missouri was down 31 at halftime. Drinkwitz called it “not a good plan offensively or defensively,” and the Tigers went 2-for-11 on third down. Missouri 2026 Results W 54-14 vs. Arkansas-Pine Bluff W 38-21 vs. Kansas W 27-17 vs. Troy L 31-24 at Mississippi State W 45-17 vs. Florida W 27-6 vs. Texas A&M L 31-3 at Ole Miss W 34-10 at Arkansas L 34-20 vs. Texas L 48-21 at Georgia Players to Know QB Austin Simmons: He won the job over Matt Zollers in the spring and opened the season 17 of 19 for 252 yards and four touchdowns. When he gets protection he can pick you apart. RB Ahmad Hardy: A preseason AP First Team All-American and the engine of the run game. Kentucky’s run defense has to be better than it was against Florida. RB Jamal Roberts: The second back in a deep backfield. WR Donovan Olugbode: Simmons’ favorite target and the guy they go to on third down. OL Cayden Green: A preseason Second Team All-American who anchors the line. Keys to the Game Fix the run defense. Florida ran 48 times for 211 yards and wore Kentucky down in the second half. Missouri will try the exact same thing with Hardy. If Kentucky can’t set the edge, it’s going to be a long night. Get the run game going again. Kentucky’s offense works when the run sets up Kenny Minchey. Sixty-one rushing yards won’t win in the SEC, let alone on the road at night. Attack the secondary. Pass defense has been Missouri’s weak spot all year. Georgia’s Gunner Stockton went 18 of 24 for 252 yards. Minchey needs to take his shots. Start fast. Missouri has started slow on the road and on the ropes. Kentucky has led into the second half against Alabama, Tennessee, and Florida and lost all three. The second half is where this team has to grow up. Win the turnover battle. Kentucky’s big wins this year came down to a play here and there. Simmons has been careless with the ball against good defenses. Make him pay. Our Early Prediction This one comes down to which team handles adversity better. Both are coming off back-to-back losses, and both had playoff hopes that are now gone. Missouri has the home field and is favored by almost a touchdown. Kentucky has the head coach who has won close games all year. What gives me some hope is the bounce back. After Alabama blew them out, the Cats went on the road and beat Texas A&M. Stein has had a whole week to get this team’s attention after being called out for not looking like themselves. I think Kentucky responds. It won’t be pretty, but the Cats grind out a road win and stay alive for a 10-win season. Download the new SB Nation app All of your communities in one place. The 6-foot-4, 300-pound defensive lineman transferred to Missouri after spending his freshman season at Miami. He appeared in eight games for the Hurricanes in 2025, recording four tackles and 1.5 tackles for loss without managing a sack. Simpson has made considerable progress since joining the Tigers. Despite missing more than a month during the offseason because of an illness that also delayed his participation in fall camp, he has emerged as one of Missouri’s most productive defensive players. I know rivalry games can make records look meaningless, and the Golden Bears would love nothing more than to keep their neighbors out of a bowl game. But at some point, I have to back the team that's actually moving in the right direction. Stanford has won three of its last four, while Cal has lost four straight and looks completely out of answers under Tosh Lupoi. The Cardinal can become bowl eligible for the first time since 2018, and I think they're playing with the urgency to make that happen. What's changed for Stanford is that the offense finally has something it can lean on. Micah Ford has rushed for at least 145 yards in three of the last four games, and he's averaging 137.5 rushing yards since the win over Elon. He just ran for 149 yards and three touchdowns in a 40-22 victory at Virginia Tech. That's a big deal against a Cal defense allowing 186.2 rushing yards per game. Stanford hasn't been a great rushing team over the entire season, but Ford's recent form gives the Cardinal a way to control possessions instead of asking Davis Warren to do everything. Warren has quietly done a nice job protecting the football. He's thrown for 2,406 yards with 14 touchdowns and only three interceptions, despite ranking among the national leaders in pass attempts. Stanford is still converting just 31.7 percent of its third downs, so it's not as though every offensive problem has disappeared. But when you can get the running game going and avoid handing the opponent short fields, you give yourself a much better chance to win close games. That's been missing from this program for a while. Cal's offense is the bigger concern for me. The Bears are scoring just 20.4 points per game and averaging only 78.7 rushing yards. That's an awful lot of pressure on Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele, who's thrown 11 touchdowns against eight interceptions. Chase Hendricks has been productive with 65 catches, but defenses don't have to respect the run nearly enough. Cal managed seven points at Virginia last week, and that loss followed defeats to Wake Forest , SMU and NC State. Those four losses have come by at least three touchdowns apiece. That's not a team that's simply catching a few unlucky breaks. I won't pretend Stanford is some defensive powerhouse. The Cardinal allow 35.8 points and nearly 449 yards per game, numbers that give Cal a legitimate opportunity to move the ball. But Stanford forced three turnovers against Virginia Tech, with Charlie Eckhardt recording two interceptions and a forced fumble. That was the Cardinal's first road win since 2024, snapping a 15-game skid away from home. The defense doesn't suddenly become great because of one afternoon, but there are signs of improvement when the offense gives it a chance. The travel angle is another reason I don't mind the road favorite here. Stanford has been crushed on several cross-country trips since joining the ACC, but going from Palo Alto to Berkeley is hardly the same situation. Cal also returns home after three straight road games, so maybe getting back to its own building helps. They haven't played in Berkeley since October 17, so there's some uncertainty there. The Bears have won the last two Big Games played in Berkeley, and that matters in a rivalry. Stanford, though, took back the Axe with a 31-10 win last season. Now there's a bowl bid waiting on the other side of another rivalry victory, while Cal is already eliminated from postseason consideration. Chris Ruffolo's Pick: Stanford -2.5 Need More? away.headline: Cal-Stanford injury report: Several key Bears players questionable
away.blurb: Although there are no new Cal players listed as being out, four starters are listed as questionable. Starting wide receiver Ian Strong, who missed last week's game, as well as defensive back Daniel Harris, safety Isaiah Crosby and inside linebacker JD McKinley are the four Cal starters listed as questionable. Safety Aiden Manutai, outside linebacker Justin Beadles and defensive lineman Ashun Shepphard are also Cal players expected to get playing time if they are healthy, but all three are listed as questionable. Also of interest is the fact that quarterback Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele and running back Adam Mohammed are listed as probable. That indicates they are likely to play against Stanford, but it also suggests they are nursing some injuries. Three Cal players listed as being out for the Big Game are the same players who have been sidelined for virtually the entire season -- running back Carter Vargas, defensive lineman Nate Burrell and tight end Dorian Thomas. This article was originally published on www.si.com/college/cal as Cal-Stanford Injury Report: Several Key Bears Players Questionable . The initial injury report for Saturday's Cal-Stanford game was released Wednesday night, and a number of key Cal players are listed. Strong is the Bears' second-leading receiver with 35 catches for 478 yards, while McKinley, who also missed last week's game, is the team's co-leader in sacks with three. Crosby is second on the team in tackles with 56 and he also has an interception and two tackles for loss. Harris is fifth on the team in tackles with 37, and he also has three tackles for loss and four quarterback hurries. Cal is 3-7 overall and is riding a four-game losing streak. The Bears will host Stanford (5-5, 4-5 ACC) in Saturday's Big Game starting at 4:30 p.m. The Cardinal would become bowl-eligible if it beats Cal. The Cardinal will continue to look for quarterback Davis Warren and running back Micah Ford to spearhead the offense against the Golden Bears. Ford is coming off a big workload against the Hokies, rushing for 149 yards on 27 carries and scoring three touchdowns. He's surpassed 100 yards in three of the past four games, leaving him 100 yards short of 1,000 for the season. Stanford safety Charlie Eckhardt will attempt to lead the defense after finishing with two interceptions, a forced fumble, a sack and a season-high 10 tackles against Virginia Tech. "Absolutely relentless effort and attitude all the time," Pritchard said of Eckhardt. "He loves to play football. He loves practicing football. He just exudes everything we want about competition and effort and relentlessness and self-improvement. Chuck embodies so much of what we want to be in this program, and I'm just so happy for him." Cal quarterback Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele threw two more interceptions last weekend to give him eight on the season. He was sacked a season-high four times. The Horned Frogs get their first shot at that sixth win Saturday, Nov. 21, when undefeated No. 2 Utah comes to Fort Worth for the home finale. Kickoff is set for 8 p.m. CT on FOX. The Horned Frogs enter at 5–5 overall and 3–4 in the Big 12. Utah is 10–0 and 7–0 in conference play. If TCU pulls off the upset Saturday, it’s bowl eligible. Otherwise, the Frogs will have one more chance on Thanksgiving at No. 12 Texas Tech. Both opponents held their spots in Tuesday’s College Football Playoff rankings. Utah needed a late touchdown to beat Arizona 40–39 in Tucson last week. Quarterback Devon Dampier accounted for four touchdowns and rushed for 100 yards, so the Frogs will have their hands full even when a play breaks down. College Football Picks, Predictions New Mexico State +3.5 Old Dominion +14 Purdue +6 vs. Wisconsin 12 p.m. ET ⋅ NBC Betting Purdue against Wisconsin …what could possibly go wrong? The Badgers have absolutely dominated this series since 2004 when Purdue blew a 17-7 fourth-quarter lead at home in a top-10 matchup in which Wisconsin capped off the comeback with a game-winning scoop-and-score in the final minutes. The Boilermakers have lost 18 straight to the Badgers in a streak that includes a 3-15 ATS (16.7%) stretch with an absurd average cover margin of -9.5 points. Over that span, Wisconsin has gone 8-0 SU and ATS in Ross-Ade Stadium. What does that have to do with this year's matchup? Nothing really, but it's still a pretty stunning stretch. I actually think Purdue has a shot at ending the long losing streak on Saturday, as I'm just not sure where Wisconsin is at mentally after blowing a touchdown lead in the final minutes last week at Maryland, which started a backup quarterback. I'm also concerned about where the Badgers are physically. They're beat up along the offensive line and will be missing two of their best defensive backs who suffered injuries last week in College Park. The offense is completely in the tank. Last week, Wisconsin didn't even throw for 100 yards, while its nonexistent run game (112th EPA) averaged just 3.3 yards per carry. The Purdue defense has holes all over, but I'm not sure the Badgers can fully exploit those deficiencies, regardless of who plays quarterback. Freshman Ryan Hopkins recently took over for Colton Joseph, who was benched due to ineffectiveness. Hopkins suffered an injury last week, so head coach Luke Fickell may turn back to Joseph, who just doesn't have great receivers to lean on and loves to put the ball in harm's way. It also doesn't help that the offensive line is now nowhere close to 100%. The Wisconsin defense has carried the team for most of the season. The linebackers are particularly stout against the run, but Purdue can't run the ball anyway. So, it will be up to quarterback Ryan Browne to attack this shorthanded Wisconsin secondary that has been much more vulnerable against the pass (71st in Success Rate). This offense has shown flashes this year against top-tier competition. The Boilermakers put up 38 and 36 earlier this season against a pair of potential playoff teams in UCLA and Wake Forest, respectively. I believe they can have enough success through the air to keep this game close throughout. Plus, I have no qualms with fading this anemic Wisconsin offense as a road favorite. Lastly, Purdue (which has played one of the 10 most difficult schedules in the country to date) has quietly had one of the best special teams units in the country to date, while Wisconsin has been merely average in that department. That could ultimately swing the game and/or cover in its favor. Purdue vs. Wisconsin Trend Since 2005, Purdue has been one of the worst teams in the country to back at home. Amazingly, the Boilermakers have gone 48-83-1 ATS (36.6%) over that span vs. FBS foes, failing to cover by nearly four points per game on average. No team in college football has been less profitable in their home building. However, Fickell is just 8-14 ATS (36.4%) as road chalk in league play since becoming a head coach, including a pair of outright losses this season to Maryland and Minnesota. He's also failed to cover by 3.3 points per game on average. Something has to give! (Photo by Patrick Mulligan/Getty Images) (Patrick Mulligan/Getty Images) Delayna Zepeda · Dallas Morning News Thu, November 19, 2026 at 12:00 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads No. 2 Utah at TCU 8 p.m. Saturday at Amon G. Carter Stadium, Fort Worth TCU (5–5, 3–4 Big 12), Utah (10–0, 7–0) TCU defeated Utah on the road in 2024, 13-7 What's at stake? The TCU Horned Frogs will face one of their toughest challenges of the season Saturday when they host No. 2 Utah at Amon G. Carter Stadium. The Frogs are coming off a 20-10 victory over Kansas State , while the Utes enter the matchup looking to keep their undefeated season alive. Utah is 10-0 overall and 7-0 in Big 12 play. Saturday's matchup will mark the highest-ranked opponent to visit Amon G. Carter Stadium since No. 2 Texas in 1970. It also marks TCU's final home game of the season before the Frogs travel to face Texas Tech on Thanksgiving Day. With a win, TCU would secure bowl eligibility and pull off one of the biggest upsets of the college football season. When TCU has the ball Quarterback Jaden Craig will be a key factor in TCU's ability to keep up with Utah's offense. Craig has thrown for 2,664 yards, 13 touchdowns and seven interceptions this season. He is coming off a 225-yard performance against Kansas State, where he also threw a touchdown pass. The Horned Frogs will need to find ways to create offensive opportunities without relying entirely on Craig's arm. Establishing the run game and finding success on early downs will be important against a Utah defense that has helped the Utes remain undefeated. Craig has also been dealing with an ankle injury that has limited his mobility. However, head coach Sonny Dykes said during Tuesday's midweek news conference that Craig is showing improvement and is expected to play Saturday. "I would expect him to play. He was a lot better today than he was yesterday. I would anticipate him being able to practice tomorrow and play on Saturday," Dykes said Tuesday. TCU will need to sustain drives, limit mistakes and take advantage of its scoring opportunities if it hopes to pull off the upset. The Frogs showed they can do that with their 20-10 victory over Kansas State. When Kansas State has the ball Undefeated Utah has been one of the strongest teams in the Big 12 this season and is looking to secure a spot in the conference championship game. The Utes will be one of TCU's toughest defensive challenges yet. The Frogs will need to limit Utah's scoring opportunities and find ways to slow down its offense if they hope to keep the game competitive. Quarterback Devon Dampier has completed 66.5% of his passes for 2,257 yards, 22 touchdowns and eight interceptions this season. His ability to make plays through the air will put pressure on TCU's secondary. TCU's defense will need to create pressure, limit big plays and force Utah into difficult third-down situations. If the Frogs cannot slow down Dampier and the Utes' offense, it could be a long night for the defense. This will be one of the toughest games of the season for the Horned Frogs. TCU is coming off a big win over Kansas State and will be hungry to prove it can compete with one of the best teams in the country. While I expect the Frogs to put up a fight, they have struggled to perform consistently under pressure this season. Utah has remained undefeated for a reason, and its strength on both sides of the ball will make this a difficult matchup for TCU. I expect the Horned Frogs to compete early, but Utah's consistency will ultimately be too much to overcome. Utah 34, TCU 14 This article originally published at Prediction for No. 2 Utah at TCU: Horned Frogs face tall task against Utes .

Utah (10-0, 7-0 Big 12) survived one of the wildest games of the season last weekend, escaping Arizona with a thrilling 40-39 victory. The Utes have now won 10 consecutive games and need just one more victory to secure their place in Arlington. Meanwhile, TCU (5-5, 3-4 Big 12) is coming off a 20-10 victory over Kansas State. The Horned Frogs are one win away from bowl eligibility, but they'll have to earn it against either Utah or Texas Tech in their final two games. Can Utah keep its perfect season alive, or will TCU deliver another Big 12 After Dark surprise? Here's everything you need to know about Utah vs. TCU, including betting odds, injury updates, the biggest question and our prediction. Carter Stadium, Fort Worth, Texas Point Spread: Utah -6.5 Over/Under: 45.5 Odds are from BetMGM on November 17 and are subject to change. Utah vs. TCU Injury Report Utah: Running back Wayshawn Parker was limited against Arizona after dealing with a heel injury. His availability and workload will be worth monitoring heading into Saturday. TCU: This will be updated as needed Biggest Question for Utah vs. TCU: Utah's Run Game vs. TCU's Run Defense The Utah Utes rank third in the Big 12 Conference in rushing yards per game at over 223. But now the Utes hit the road and take on the stingiest run defense in the Big 12, with TCU leading the way in the Big 12 in only allowing 109 rushing yards per game, 10 yards better than anyone else in the conference. How does Devon Dampier, Wayshawn Parker/Daniel Bray handle the ground game, which they will want to get going on the road to stay undefeated? That's the biggest question of the game and will determine whether or not an upset might be in store. Utah vs. TCU Pick and Prediction TCU is 5-5, but every loss has been by one score. That's a testament to this defense, not so much the offense. They have the top scoring defense in the Big 12 this season, and rank second in total defense as well. But here's the thing, TCU's defensive numbers may be skewed in part by who they have, and haven't played, thus far this season. They wrap up the season playing Utah and Texas Tech, two of the more explosive offenses in the Big 12. And the other part of this that concerns me for TCU: Even if the defense holds its own, does it just get worn down as the game progresses, especially if TCU's offense can't get it going? TCU will and can put up an admirable fight, but I don't see it resulting in a win or a cover. Utah is 8-2 against the spread this year, and it'll be 9-2 come Saturday in Fort Worth. Utah can secure its spot in the Big 12 Championship Game with a victory over TCU. The Utes enter Week 12 undefeated in conference play at 7-0. Can TCU still become bowl eligible? Yes.
